item.title: The Koto II experiment
item.dc:creator: Silvia Martellotti
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

K_L →π⁰νν̅ is a golden mode for flavour physics: it is highly suppressed in the Standard Model, with a predicted branching ratio of 3 ×10⁻¹¹ and a theoretical uncertainty of just 2\%, and is therefore extremely sensitive to new physics. The KOTO experiment at J-PARC is searching for this decay. Using the data taken in 2021, it has set the most stringent upper limit to date of 2.2 ×10⁻⁹ on the branching ratio at 90\% C.L. We present KOTO II, a next-generation experiment at J-PARC proposed in 2024, which aims to measure the K_L →π⁰νν̅ branching ratio with a sensitivity below 10⁻¹² in the 2030s.

item.title: GeoRead: Geometry-Aware Transformer for Continuous AC-LGAD Readout Reconstruction
item.dc:creator: Lixing Wang et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) are promising silicon sensor technologies for high-precision four-dimensional tracking. Position reconstruction in AC-LGADs relies on correlations among waveforms induced on multiple readout pads, where analytically solving the signal propagation becomes difficult, motivating data-based machine learning reconstruction. Existing machine learning approaches generally assume a fixed readout pad layout and predict one hit from an isolated, temporally aligned waveform window. These assumptions limit their flexibility across sensor designs and applicability to continuous readout where signal arrival times are not known in advance and multiple hits might overlap in the same waveforms. We introduce GeoRead, a spatial-temporal Transformer enabling multi-event continuous position prediction and uncertainty estimation. We incorporate relative pad positions into attention and produces time-resolved hit position estimates with predictive uncertainties. Time-jitter and additive event-mixing augmentations are used to train the model on temporally misaligned and overlapping waveforms synthesized from single-event measurements. Using four-channel transient-current-technique (TCT) data of a 500\mum-pitch AC-LGAD, GeoRead achieves median position errors of 5.8\mum within the convex hull of the readout-pad centers and 8.2\mum over the full scanned region at 190\volt. The model maintains comparable accuracy under temporal shifts and demonstrates time-resolved reconstruction of superposed events, without predefined per-event window. These results provide a basis for extending waveform-based position reconstruction toward continuous readout and flexible sensor geometries.

item.title: Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data
item.dc:creator: V. Aushev et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The reconstruction of the top-quark-pair (tt̅) kinematics in the dilepton tt̅ decay channel is challenging due to the presence of two undetected neutrinos. In this work, existing kinematic reconstruction methods used by the CMS Collaboration are studied using a Monte Carlo sample with tt̅ events from CMS Open Data at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. An improved version of the loose kinematic reconstruction, LKRv2, is developed by imposing more stringent requirements on the jet-lepton pairing entering the reconstruction. A further modification, LKRv3, exploits the kinematic similarity between the dilepton and neutrino-pair systems and improves the resolution of the reconstructed tt̅ invariant mass relative to the baseline LKR by 7%, with smaller improvements for the transverse momentum and rapidity of tt̅. In addition, two machine-learning (ML) based approaches are developed using a residual multilayer perceptron and a conditional normalizing flow. Relative to LKRv3, they improve the resolution of the invariant mass, transverse momentum and rapidity by approximately 30%, 20% and 15%, respectively. In particular, a resolution of 30 GeV is achieved for the reconstructed invariant mass of tt̅ near the production threshold. A dedicated generator-level study and a generator-to-detector transfer test demonstrate that the ML approaches learn a genuine physics-driven correction to the νν̅ approximation, rather than merely exploiting detector-specific effects. These results demonstrate the strong potential of ML-based approaches for improving the reconstruction of dilepton tt̅ events, while identifying the neutrino-pair approximation as an important limitation on the achievable resolution.

item.title: Amplitude Analysis of the Invariant-Mass Spectra of Centrally Exclusively Produced π⁺π⁻ and K⁺K⁻ Pairs in pp Collisions at √(s)=510 GeV
item.dc:creator: Aranya Giri et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present an amplitude analysis of the π⁺π⁻ and K⁺K⁻ invariant-mass spectra from central exclusive pp collisions at √(s)=510 GeV, measured by the STAR experiment with forward-scattered protons tagged in the Roman Pot detectors. The π⁺π⁻ channel is described with f_0(500), ρ⁰⁽⁷⁷⁰⁾, f_0(980), f_2(1270), f_0(1500) and f_0(1710) resonances with χ²/ndf=121.712/57. The fit also yields m_f_0(980)=0.989 GeV and Γ=0.091 GeV. The K⁺K⁻ channel is described with f_0(980), f_2(1270), f_2^’(1525) and f_0(1710) resonances with χ²/ndf=14.662/15. The fiducial cross sections for the individual resonances and interference terms were calculated, together with their ratios relative to the total fitted cross section. These ratios were compared across decay channels and qualitatively with previous measurements. A consistent flavor dependence of f_0(1500) and f_0(1710) has been derived for the highest RHIC collision energies, which is in agreement with low energy data.

item.title: First broadband search for fixed-polarization dark photon dark matter with GigaBREAD
item.dc:creator: Jialin Yu et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present the first search for fixed-polarization dark photon (DP) dark matter in the 44-52μeV mass range, corresponding to 10.7-12.5GHz. GigaBREAD is a room-temperature broadband dish antenna experiment in which DP convert to ordinary photons on a cylindrical metallic emission surface and are focused onto a radio-frequency receiver. Previous searches, including GigaBREAD and several other dish antenna searches, have assumed randomly polarized DP dark matter. However, vector dark matter produced by a misalignment-like mechanism may retain an approximately fixed polarization, leading to sidereal modulation of the detector response as the Earth rotates. We reanalyze the GigaBREAD data using a polarization-matched likelihood that accounts for the time-dependent projection of a fixed DP polarization onto the detector axis. We find no evidence for a fixed-polarization DP signal and set upper limits on the kinetic mixing parameter at the level of χ∼10⁻¹². These limits are about 20% better than a naive limit obtained by rescaling the previous GigaBREAD limit under the fixed-polarization assumption.

item.title: Search for dark matter axions at 1-2 micro-eV with a RADES-DarkQuantum haloscope at CERN
item.dc:creator: Alberto Arcusa Puente et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The QCD axion remains one of the most compelling candidates for the dark matter of the Universe, yet the mass range around 1\text{–}\SI{2}{\micro\electronvolt} remains essentially unexplored. In this paper, we describe a proposal to employ CERN’s M1 superconducting magnet to deploy a haloscope to perform a search for galactic axion and axion-like particle dark matter providing continuous coverage from approximately 1.2 to 1.8 \SI{}{\micro\electronvolt}. Under conservative assumptions, the experiment can reach the QCD axion band over a significant fraction of the scanned range, while optimistic detector performance would allow sensitivity to benchmark models such as KSVZ and DFSZ over a large part of the explored mass interval. With the current long shut-down of CERN’s accelerators providing a unique and timely window, such an experiment will deliver high-impact results even in conservative scenarios and potentially delivering a definitive test of the axion dark matter paradigm in the unexplored 1\text{–}\SI{2}{\micro\electronvolt} mass range.

item.title: Data-quality monitoring of luminosity blocks with ATLAS Open Data: an open benchmark and a learned within-run detector
item.dc:creator: Renjie Wang
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Data-quality monitoring at the LHC decides, luminosity block by luminosity block, which collision data enter physics analyses, yet its methods cannot be compared openly because the experiments’ monitoring data are not public. We construct a public benchmark from the ATLAS Open Data release of the 2015–2016 proton–proton collisions at √(s)=13~TeV: 1289-bin histograms of reconstructed jets, electrons, photons, muons and the missing transverse momentum computed from them, for 39\,828 luminosity blocks of all 217 runs in the Good Run Lists; eight types of detector defects injected at event level at three strengths; real-data labels from the Good Run Lists and the liquid-argon calorimeter error flag; and a time-ordered protocol in which every detector is trained and calibrated on earlier runs only. Histogram shapes differ far more between runs than within a run (median χ²/n_dof of 5.9 against 1.1), so references and autoencoders built across runs fail, and all competitive detectors use residuals with respect to a robust reference of each run. A gradient-boosted classifier on position-invariant features of these residuals, trained on synthetic defects and calibrated by split-conformal prediction, detects 43\% of the luminosity blocks with injected defects at a false-positive rate of 1.0\%, against 25\% for a matched-filter scan and 63\% for a single-histogram test that knows the defect pattern. For defect types excluded from its training, its efficiency falls to 18\%; adding pattern-agnostic synthetic detector failures to the training raises it to 34\%, above the scan, at a cost of three percentage points on the known types.

item.title: Commissioning and Performance of the LHCb Upstream Tracker
item.dc:creator: D. Andreou et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The Upstream Tracker is a new, high-precision silicon strip detector installed in the LHCb experiment as part of the overall LHCb Upgrade I project. The detector is an integral part of the tracking system, and plays a crucial role in the reconstruction of charged particles in the new fully software-based trigger. An overview of the Upstream Tracker detector design, its commissioning, and performance are presented.

item.title: Development and performance of a transformer-based lepton isolation algorithm with the ATLAS experiment
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The Prompt Lepton Isolation Tagger (PLIT) is a transformer-based algorithm designed to distinguish prompt leptons (electrons and muons) produced in the primary decays of electroweak gauge bosons from non-prompt leptons produced in hadron decays and from misidentified leptons. It is primarily used in measurements targeting multilepton final states with important backgrounds from non-prompt and misidentified leptons. PLIT exploits information from charged-particle tracks associated with the lepton candidate, together with lepton properties, using a transformer neural network to identify correlations between the tracks and improve the discrimination. Its performance is evaluated using simulated top-quark pair production events and compared with that of previously used lepton isolation algorithms, demonstrating improved prompt lepton efficiency while maintaining high rejection of non-prompt leptons. This article presents the development, performance, and calibration of PLIT for electrons and muons in proton–proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of √(s)=13.6 TeV recorded by the ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. Operating points are defined for both electrons and muons, and their efficiencies are calibrated using Z→l⁺l⁻ events in Run 3 data, providing data-to-simulation correction factors for physics analyses.

item.title: Search for Higgs boson production in association with another Higgs or an exotic scalar boson in the bb̅W⁺W⁻ single lepton final state at √(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS experiment
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A search for Higgs boson pair production where one Higgs boson decays via H →b b̅ and the other Higgs boson decays via H →WW^*→ℓνq q̅ (ℓ=e,μ) is presented. This search uses the complete Run 2 data sample recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC from 2015 to 2018 at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb⁻¹. The analysis looks for non-resonant Higgs boson pair production assuming Standard Model dynamics. No evidence for Higgs-boson pair production is observed and an upper limit at 95% confidence level is set at 35 times the Standard Model prediction. The same selection is used to target Beyond the Standard Model theories predicting the resonant production of the heavy scalars, X and S, with m_X > m_S > m_H, undergoing the process X →SH, S →W⁺W⁻, H →b b̅. Limits are set on the resonant X →SH production for several combinations of the two scalar’s masses within the m_X mass range 350-3000 GeV and m_S mass range 170-2500 GeV.

item.title: Measurements of isolated photon pair production in association with jets in pp collisions at √(s) = 8 TeV with the ATLAS detector
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Measurements of integrated and differential production cross section of two isolated photons in events with and without associated hadronic jets based on the 2012 dataset of 20.3 fb⁻¹ integrated luminosity of proton-proton collisions at √(s)=8 TeV collected by the ATLAS experiment are presented. The measurements consider photons with pseudorapidities of |η^γ|<1.37 or 1.56<|η^γ|<2.37 and transverse energy of E_T^γ>22 GeV. Jets are required to have p_T^j>25 GeV for |η^j|<2.4 and p_T^j>50 GeV for 2.4<|η^j|<4.4. Events are classified into categories based on the number of jets and integrated fiducial cross sections of diphoton production in association with inclusive and exclusive number of jets are presented. Fiducial cross sections, differential in sixteen diphoton, jet, dijet and photon-jet observables, are presented and compared with leading-order Sherpa 1.4.1 predictions in all jet categories, fixed-order next-to-leading-order GoSam and BlackHat calculations in selected categories, and NLO-matched predictions from Sherpa 2.2.14 in all categories. Overall, the NLO predictions provide a reasonable description of the data, with significant discrepancies observed for increasing jet multiplicity, particularly for angular variables, attributable to the absence of higher-order terms in the calculations. The Sherpa 2.2.14 NLO-matched predictions provide the best overall description of the data across all jet categories and observables.

item.title: Operational Challenges in Efficient and Sustainable Operation of the Event Processing Nodes GPU Farm at the ALICE Experiment
item.dc:creator: Federico Ronchetti et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

ALICE’s Event Processing Nodes (EPN) farm is CERN’s largest GPU computing facility by capacity, comprising 350 GPU-based nodes and 2800 GPUs delivering approximately a total of 48\,PFLOP/s. It has successfully enabled real-time processing of heavy-ion collisions at 50\,kHz during LHC Run~3. The facility was designed for sustainability, extended hardware lifetime, and reduced operational overhead. High availability is supported by a robust technical architecture and well-defined operational practices, ensuring reliable and continuous operation throughout data taking.

item.title: Constraints on a Long-Lived X17 Vector Boson with FASER
item.dc:creator: FASER Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The ATOMKI anomalies motivate the possibility of a new particle, the X17, with a mass of 17 MeV and weak couplings to nuclei and electrons. Such a particle may be produced at the LHC, travel 480 m in the far-forward direction, and decay to e⁺e⁻ in FASER. In this paper, previous FASER searches for dark photons and axion-like particles (ALPs) are combined and interpreted as searches for a candidate X17 particle, the protophobic vector boson. The searches use data collected from pp collisions at √(s) = 13.6 TeV in LHC Run 3 from 2022 for the dark photon search and from 2022-2023 for the ALP search. No excess events are found above the expected background, and the combined null results exclude a previously-unconstrained “low-coupling window” with electron coupling 6 ×10⁻⁵ < ϵ_e < 1.2 ×10⁻⁴. A “high-coupling window” remains.

item.title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
item.dc:creator: Aim\'e Matheron et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The superposition principle at the heart of optics states that electromagnetic fields do not interact in vacuum. This principle is not universal, instead electromagnetic fields couple weakly via quantum vacuum fluctuations. Striking consequences are light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence. Experimental results from colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers combined with dark-field detection and polarimetry for background suppression are reported. This approach yields the most stringent bound for light-by-light scattering in the low-energy regime achieved to date – improving upon previous experimental limits by ten orders of magnitude – and paves the way for precision measurements.

item.title: A New Precise Measurement of the e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻⁽γ) Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
item.dc:creator: BaBar Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We measure the e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻⁽γ) cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb⁻¹ of BaBar initial-state radiation data. The result is obtained from the π⁺π⁻/μ⁺μ⁻ ratio, reducing systematic uncertainties that are in common. Unlike the previous 2009 BaBar analysis, the pion and muon contributions are separated statistically through their angular distributions. The compatibility with the previous BaBar result is quantified including statistical and systematic correlations. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results as a function of energy and in terms of its hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly. The leading-order HVP contribution of the two-pion channel in the energy range of 0.3-1.4 GeV is a_μ^ππ=525.9±3.5_stat±3.8_syst and 517.8±2.4_stat±3.3_syst in units of 10⁻¹⁰ for the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements, respectively.

item.title: A New Precise Measurement of the e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻⁽γ) Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
item.dc:creator: BaBar Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We report precise results for the e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻⁽γ) cross section in the energy range between threshold and 1.4 GeV, relevant for the hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon g-2 prediction. Using the full 460 fb⁻¹ of on- and off-Υ(4S) data, the cross section is derived from the ratio of π⁺π⁻ to μ⁺μ⁻ initial-state radiation (ISR) events, in which many systematic uncertainties cancel. The pion/muon separation does not rely on particle identification as in the 2009 BaBar analysis, but rather makes use of the well-known, different angular distributions in the two-particle center-of-mass system. The compatibility and correlation between the 2026 and 2009 measurements are discussed. The new measurement is also compared with other two-pion results. The leading-order hadronic contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly calculated using the new 2026 and combined 2009 and 2026 BaBar measurements in the energy range of 0.3-1.4 GeV are 525.9±3.5_stat±3.8_syst and 517.8±2.4_stat±3.3_syst in units of 10⁻¹⁰, respectively.

item.title: Search for heavy neutral leptons in top quark decays with same-sign, same-flavor dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at √(s) = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A search for a Majorana-type heavy neutral lepton (HNL) produced in top quark decays is reported. The search is based on proton-proton collision data at √(s) = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb⁻¹, collected during 2016-2018 with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC. In the type-I seesaw model, a Majorana HNL can mediate lepton-number-violating top quark decays. The search targets top quark pair production events in which one top quark decays into a bottom quark and a W boson, which subsequently decays into a charged lepton (electron or muon) and an HNL. The Majorana HNL then decays into a W boson and a charged lepton with the same sign and flavor as the one produced with the HNL. The experimental signature features a same-sign, same-flavor lepton pair and jets. The HNL masses between 20 and 100 GeV are probed. The data agree with the standard model background prediction. Observed (expected) upper limits at 95% confidence level are set on the branching fraction of the top quark decay into an HNL, a charged lepton, and a bottom quark, varying between [1.1 (0.71)] ×10⁻⁵ and [4.8 (3.0)] ×10⁻⁵ in the dielectron channel, and between [3.7 (3.4)] ×10⁻⁶ and [2.4 (1.3)] ×10⁻⁵ in the dimuon channel.

item.title: Projected sensitivity of the \anubis detector to photophobic and fermion-coupled axion-like particles
item.dc:creator: Riley Aumonier et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Axion-like particles (ALPs) are a common benchmark for experiments at the lifetime frontier, as their suppressed couplings to Standard Model particles can render them long-lived on detector scales. This article presents the projected sensitivity of the ANUBIS detector at the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) to two scenarios: a photophobic ALP model and a modified version of the flavour-diagonal, fermion-coupled ALP benchmark of the Physics Beyond Colliders initiative that introduces an additional h→Za decay. For the photophobic case, the ANUBIS detector will reach a peak sensitivity of σ_Wa·Br(a→gg)=6.2×10⁻⁴~pb at cτ=1.95 m for an ALP mass of 10 GeV. This will improve on the current exclusion limits from the ATLAS experiment by two orders of magnitude and extend the cτ coverage by three orders of magnitude. For the fermion-coupled case with a dimension-seven Higgs–ALP interaction, the peak sensitivity to the fermion coupling is C_a^Φ=4.4×10⁻⁸, reached for ALP masses between 16 and 23 GeV. Overall, the ANUBIS detector is shown to provide unique coverage of the parameter space of both models, in regions that can be probed neither by the main LHC experiments nor by forward detectors at the HL-LHC.

item.title: Search for GeV-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A search is performed for the production of axion-like particles with masses in the range 3-10 GeV using PbPb collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 0.228 nb⁻¹ and a nucleon-nucleon centre-of-mass energy of √(s_NN)=5.02 TeV. This is the first search for axion-like particles produced exclusively by two photons (γγ→a→γγ) in the forward direction. It extends sensitivity to previously unexplored regions of the parameter space, probing axion-like particle masses and couplings down to 3.0 GeV and 3.2×10⁻⁴ GeV⁻¹, respectively. This result provides the most stringent limits to date on the production of axion-like particles from exclusive photon-photon fusion processes with masses between 3 and 5 GeV.

item.title: Evidence for the decay B⁰ →μ⁺ μ⁻ and improved measurements of the decay B⁰_s →μ⁺ μ⁻
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The first single-experiment evidence for the rare decay B⁰ →μ⁺ μ⁻ and the world’s most precise measurements of the B⁰_s →μ⁺ μ⁻ branching fraction and effective lifetime are reported. The results are obtained using Run 3 proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 18 fb⁻¹ recorded with the LHCb Upgrade I detector at a centre-of-mass energy of 13.6 TeV between 2024 and 2025. Their combination with the Run 1 and Run 2 LHCb results further improves the precision. All measurements are found to be in agreement with the Standard Model expectations.

item.title: Heavy Quarkonium Physics: An Experimental Review at Tevatron, LHC, and e+e- Colliders
item.dc:creator: Zhipeng Cui et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We review recent experimental advances in heavy quarkonium physics at the Tevatron, e+e- colliders (Belle, BaBar, Belle II, BESIII, and LEP), and the LHC (ALICE, ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb), including Run 2 and early Run 3 results. Differential cross sections and polarization measurements of charmonium (Jpsi, Psi(2S)) and bottomonium (Upsilon(nS)) test perturbative and non-perturbative QCD within the Non-Relativistic QCD (NRQCD) framework and probe symmetry relations among spin and orbital configurations. CDF and D0 established production baselines and exposed polarization tensions with early NRQCD predictions. Complementary e+e- measurements provide precise spectroscopy, branching fractions, radiative and hadronic transitions, and observations of exotic quarkonium-like states, constraining non-perturbative dynamics. LHC measurements extend production and polarization studies across broad kinematic ranges. Spectroscopic advances include fully-heavy tetraquark candidates, exotic structures in Jpsi Jpsi and Jpsi Psi(2S) reported by LHCb, and studies of toponium (ttbar) quasi-bound states. Sequential bottomonium suppression in PbPb collisions probes the quark-gluon plasma, while pPb measurements constrain cold nuclear matter effects. Multi-quarkonium production explores multi-parton interactions and exotic-hadron structure. Together, these results establish heavy quarkonium as a laboratory for QCD and a probe for physics beyond the Standard Model, while highlighting unresolved theoretical challenges. Future programs at the LHC, Belle II, and BESIII promise greater precision and new discoveries.

item.title: LHμC Concept: Energy-Frontier Antimuon-Proton Collisions at CERN
item.dc:creator: Arda Goroglu et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The concept of the LHμC, an energy-frontier antimuon-proton collider based on the HL-LHC, is presented. After recalling why energy-frontier lepton-hadron colliders are indispensable as QCD explorers and reviewing the history of muon-proton collider proposals, two ways of realising μp collisions at the LHC are compared: with muon-collider beams and with ultra-cold μ⁺ beams as proposed for μTRISTAN. For the latter, a μTRISTAN-type booster and the re-use of the LHeC energy-recovery-linac tunnel are discussed; colliding 1 TeV antimuons with 7 TeV protons gives √(s)=5.3 TeV and peak luminosities of 8.8×10³³ and 7.2×10³³ cm⁻²s⁻¹, respectively. The detector concept and the physics potential, including searches for colour-octet muons and R-parity-violating squarks, are discussed together with the main challenges.

item.title: Measurement of the |V_cb| element of the CKM matrix using tt̅ events in pp collisions at √(s) = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A measurement of the magnitude of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element V_cb is presented using top quark pair events produced in proton-proton collisions at √(s) = 13 TeV. The data correspond to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb⁻¹ collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC. The measurement targets the lepton+jets final state, where one W boson decays leptonically and the other hadronically. The value of |V_cb| is extracted from the branching fraction of the W → cb decay. To identify this rare signal amid the dominant W → ud and W → cs backgrounds, a multivariate discriminant based primarily on the b jet tagging information of the jets assigned to the hadronic W boson decay is used. The measured value is |V_cb| = [4.59⁺⁰.44_-0.48 (stat) ⁰.64_-0.76 (syst)] × 10⁻². This measurement provides a complementary determination of |V_cb| at the electroweak scale, independent of the nonperturbative quantum chromodynamics inputs used in measurements based on semileptonic B meson decays.

item.title: World average charged-current inclusive neutrino cross section from 6 to 200 GeV
item.dc:creator: Richard Gran
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The methods of the Particle Data Group are applied to produce a world average inclusive, charged-current, muon neutrino cross section energy-dependence slope σ/E_ν . For the energy range 30 < E_ν< 200, values obtained are (0.677 ± 0.013) and (0.335 ± 0.007) ×10⁻³⁸ cm²/GeV for neutrino and anti-neutrino, respectively. These values are practically identical to those in common use. This paper expands the experiments whose data are used and describes the evolution of measurements leading to the result. Next, the value for σ/E_ν is obtained for the low energy extensions by experiments that used the low-ν method to anchor to the high energy result. In the range 6 < E_ν< 30 GeV, values of (0.698 ± 0.018) and (0.316 ± 0.012) ×10⁻³⁸ cm²/GeV are obtained. These are higher than the high energy average for neutrino and lower for anti-neutrino, but consistent at the edge of the uncertainty estimates. An interpretation of the evolution of the inclusive cross section, nuclear effects, and isoscalar corrections is provided in the context of the Bodek Yang 2000 model and two configurations of the GENIE neutrino event generators. These cross sections underpin foundational neutrino quantities such as structure functions, electroweak parameter measurements, and oscillation parameter determinations.

item.title: CELEBI: Design and Realization of a Reproducible Physics Analysis Framework
item.dc:creator: Mingrui Zhao
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Reproducibility in modern physics analysis requires more than preserving source code or workflow descriptions. Analyses evolve through changes in code, configurations, parameters, input datasets, and dependencies, requiring a coherent representation of both the analysis and the provenance of its results. We present Celebi, a framework for organizing and preserving evolving physics analyses while keeping analysis definitions lightweight and separate from generated data products. Celebi maintains analysis definitions and preserved states in an Analysis Repository, while execution and generated results are managed separately through a Production Factory. The middleware layer, Yuki, connects preserved analysis states to execution infrastructure by constructing executable Snakemake workflows and dispatching them to supported runners, keeping the analysis representation independent of execution backends. This paper presents three main design concepts. First, the workflow architecture provides a modular representation of analysis components and their dependencies. Second, a structured file organization realizes this model in a human-readable form, separating reusable algorithms, task-specific configurations, parameters, documentation, and dependencies into well-defined objects. Third, the impression mechanism preserves immutable states of these objects and their dependencies, assigning persistent identities to specific analysis configurations and linking generated results unambiguously to their originating states. Together, these concepts establish a coherent representation of evolving physics analyses, supporting reproducibility, provenance tracking, collaboration, and long-term preservation.

item.title: CELEBI: Towards Reproducible and FAIR Physics Analysis
item.dc:creator: Mingrui Zhao
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Modern physics analyses evolve continuously as datasets, selections, parameters, software environments, and analysis strategies are updated. Over the lifetime of an analysis, this evolution can make it difficult to determine the conditions under which an earlier result was produced or to transfer the analysis reliably between collaborators. We present Celebi, an analysis-management framework that maintains a persistent connection between evolving analysis materials and their generated results. Celebi organizes reusable algorithms, tasks, and their dependencies into a structured workflow, preserves selected states as immutable impressions, and associates retained results with the states responsible for their production. This organization supports analysis modification, systematic variations, collaboration, and review while the working analysis continues to evolve. Celebi supports controlled rerunning of preserved analysis states. When results remain retained, they can be inspected and compared together with their corresponding states. By capturing provenance during everyday analysis development, Celebi reduces the need to reconstruct analysis history retrospectively and provides a practical foundation for more transparent and reusable physics analysis.

item.title: Reinforcement Learning in High-Energy Physics: A Survey from Accelerator Control to Theory Exploration
item.dc:creator: Luca Anzalone
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Reinforcement learning (RL) is a machine learning paradigm in which an agent learns a decision-making policy by interacting with an environment, guided by a scalar reward rather than explicit supervision. Supervised and unsupervised learning have become indispensable tools in high-energy physics (HEP), but they learn from fixed datasets, whereas many HEP tasks are closed-loop decisions: the data an algorithm observes depend on its choices, the feedback is sparse or delayed, and the objective is often measured on a real machine or in a stochastic simulation, not by a differentiable model. This survey reviews the application of RL to such tasks: accelerator control and feedback, data quality monitoring, jet grooming, clustering, and representation, charged particle tracking, beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) and string model building, detector design, trigger control, analysis, and formal quantum field theory computation. It provides a self-contained introduction to the underlying RL methods, from model-free and model-based to multi-agent, offline, inverse, and bandit approaches, reviews each domain against its traditional methods, and summarizes the head-to-head comparisons. The applications range from policies deployed on real accelerators and evaluated on recorded collision data to exploratory studies in formal theory. RL is most advantageous for repeated tasks with a fast simulator, decisions inside fast control loops, operation under faults and corrupted measurements, physics-based rewards in place of labels, and sequential discrete constructions with a reusable policy, while Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, and differentiable methods remain competitive elsewhere. We conclude with the open challenges that recur across domains, including reward design, sim-to-real transfer, safety, the lack of shared benchmarks, and the statistical validity of policy-driven decisions.

item.title: Search for supersymmetric particle pair production in final states with two oppositely charged leptons and large missing transverse momentum in proton-proton collisions at √(s) = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A search is presented for direct production of pairs of supersymmetric particles in final states with a pair of oppositely charged leptons (electrons or muons) and missing transverse momentum. The analysis uses proton-proton collision data at √(s) = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb⁻¹, recorded with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC. The observed data do not exhibit any excess over the standard model predictions. Constraints are derived on chargino, top squark, and slepton pair production in the context of simplified models with R-parity conservation. In these models, the neutralino is taken to be the lightest supersymmetric particle. For chargino production, an exclusion region in the chargino-neutralino mass plane is determined, which extends to chargino masses of 1120 GeV and neutralino masses of 490 GeV. For mass splittings between the lighter top squark and the neutralino ranging from the W boson mass to the top quark mass, top squark masses up to 500-540 GeV are excluded. Slepton masses are excluded up to 700 GeV for a massless neutralino.

item.title: Experimental Searches for Muon to Electron Conversion in Nuclei
item.dc:creator: Yoshitaka Kuno
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV) provides a highly sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. This experimental review discusses μ⁻ →e⁻ conversion in nuclei, which is a muon CLFV process characterized by a clean monoenergetic-electron signature and the ability to exploit large samples of stopped muons. It describes the physics motivation, basic experimental principles, key background sources, and search strategies, as well as the status and prospects of past and next-generation experiments such as COMET and Mu2e. Future experimental concepts may extend the sensitivity even further. If a signal is observed, comparisons among results obtained with different target nuclei and with those from complementary searches for other muon CLFV decay modes will be essential for identifying the underlying interaction.

item.title: Search for dark photon dark matter near 1 𝐦𝐞𝐕 using a superconducting mixer
item.dc:creator: K. Hanimura et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We demonstrate the use of a superconducting mixer for direct searches for dark photon dark matter (DPDM) in the meV mass range. DPDM couples to the ordinary electromagnetic field through kinetic mixing with a coupling constant χ and can convert into ordinary photons at the surface of a metal plate. For DPDM masses of 1 meV, the conversion photons have frequencies of around 240 GHz. At such frequencies, superconducting mixers enable low-noise spectroscopic measurements. We performed a direct search for DPDM in the mass range 1.0047578-1.0047598 meV, corresponding to the frequency range 242.94935-242.94983 GHz, using approximately one hour of data obtained with a cryogenic millimeter-wave receiver based on a superconducting mixer. No significant excess was found, and we set upper limits of χ< (1.6-1.9)×10⁻⁹ at the 95% confidence level. These limits are comparable to existing constraints from solar dark photons. By applying this method, we plan to extend the search to the wider mass range of 0.7-1.1 meV, corresponding to 170-260 GHz, with improved sensitivity.

item.title: Study of the up-down asymmetry in B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻γ using K_1(1270) amplitudes constrained by semileptonic D Decays
item.dc:creator: Yijia Zeng et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using K_1(1270)→Kππ amplitude models constrained by the charmed-meson semileptonic decays D⁺⁽⁰⁾→K⁻π⁺π⁰⁽⁻⁾ e⁺ν_e, we present a model-dependent estimate of the up-down asymmetry observed in B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻γ in the mass region M_K⁺π⁺π⁻∈[1.1,1.3]~GeV/c². Estimates based on an isolated K_1(1270) show significant model dependence, but systematically lie below the measured asymmetry ℋ̅_ud=(0.092±0.023) when assuming λ_γ=1. We also explore interference with the K_1(1400) tail and find that it can appreciably reduce the tension.

item.title: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment
item.dc:creator: John Alison et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Final states with several jets from the decays of heavy particles pose a combinatorial problem, since the jets must be assigned, at least implicitly, to their parent particles. We describe the Combinatorial Residual Network (CoReNet), a classifier that encodes the assumed decay chain of the final state in its architecture. CoReNet builds its event representation level by level along the decay hierarchy, evaluates every jet assignment hypothesis with weights shared across objects, and combines the hypotheses with learned weights using residual networks. The exchange symmetries of the decay are built into the construction, the size of the network does not depend on the number of hypotheses, and the network is trained with the classification loss alone, without generator-level jet assignments. The architecture was developed for the bb̅bb̅ final state and has been used in several CMS searches. On fast-simulation samples of Higgs boson pair production in the bb̅bb̅ final state against QCD multijet production, CoReNet with 1508 trainable parameters performs well above kinematic baselines and trains in minutes on a single GPU. Its hypothesis weights select the truth-matched jet pairing in most of the signal events in which it is defined, although no assignment target is used in training. Since only the encoded decay chain is specific to the final state, the construction carries over to other topologies, which we test with HH →bb̅W⁺W⁻ against semileptonic tt̅. There, encoding the decay chain of the background as well as that of the signal further improves the classification, at a cost of about 10³ parameters. In both final states its performance is comparable to that of a state-of-the-art transformer-based network more than two orders of magnitude larger. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/cms-cmu/CoReNet.

item.title: Search for long-lived heavy neutral leptons in signatures with one prompt muon and a secondary vertex formed by two non-prompt muons in proton-proton collisions at √(s) = 13 and 13.6 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A search for heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) in the decay of W bosons is performed in final states with three muons, with one originating promptly from the primary interaction vertex and the other two stemming from a common secondary vertex. The analyzed proton-proton collision data correspond to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb⁻¹ recorded at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV in 2016-2018, and of 34.6 fb⁻¹ recorded at 13.6 TeV in 2022. The analysis strategy is optimized for large HNL decay lengths by requiring highly non-prompt muons forming a secondary vertex far from the beam line, and hence reconstructed only in the muon system of the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC. This enhances the analysis reach in the high HNL lifetime region, corresponding to low HNL masses (2-4 GeV) and small mixing parameters with the standard model neutrinos (10⁻⁶-10⁻⁵), where prompt and tracker-based non-prompt analyses have limited acceptance. No excess over the background prediction is found. Under the Majorana HNL hypothesis, exclusion limits at 95\% confidence level are set on the HNL mixing parameter as functions of the HNL mass in the range of 1-5 GeV.

item.title: Reconstruct everything everywhere all at once: An end-to-end model for future colliders
item.dc:creator: Max Hart et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present the Reconstruct Everything Model (REM), an end-to-end multitask model for sparse, multimodal sensor data, demonstrated in high-energy physics. To our knowledge, REM is the first demonstration of a single learned framework simultaneously reconstructing multiple particle types directly from hit-level measurements across the silicon tracker, calorimeters, and muon system in a full simulation. It performs hit assignment, particle identification, kinematic regression, and resonance reconstruction without externally reconstructed tracks or calorimeter clusters as inputs. REM improves particle-reconstruction efficiency and purity and jet-energy resolution relative to both conventional and machine-learned particle-flow approaches. In diboson events, the learned resonance reconstruction improves W/Z mass separation relative to conventional jet reconstruction. These results demonstrate a reconstruction chain from detector hits to particles to resonances, with potential applications to structured prediction in other large-scale, sparse, multimodal sensor systems.

item.title: A first look at strange-quark polarization in top-quark decays with CMS Open Data
item.dc:creator: Yevgeny Kats
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present a first realization of strange-quark polarimetry in top-quark decays. The longitudinal polarization of Λ baryons is measured in the strange jets of hadronic W→cs̅ decays in semileptonic top-quark pair events, using 16.39 fb⁻¹ of the public CMS data of pp collisions at √(s)=13 TeV. The W decay produces the strange quark fully polarized, so that the Λ polarization measures the transfer of the quark polarization in fragmentation. With the limited statistics available, our result is consistent both with zero and with the transfer inferred from the flavor-averaged LEP measurements. The statistical reach with the full Run-2, Run-3 and HL-LHC datasets is projected.

item.title: SuperJEPA: Pretraining with a Supervision-Augmented Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for High Energy Physics
item.dc:creator: Dylan Sheldon Rankin et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Foundation models often obtain powerful results through very large unlabeled training datasets that dwarf available labeled datasets in size, but high energy physics already provides large samples of high-fidelity labeled simulation. We therefore ask whether self-supervised objectives improve over supervised pretraining alone when large labeled samples already exist. We introduce SuperJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architec- ture augmented with a supervised objective, and find improved downstream jet-tagging performance across multiple tasks, model sizes, and pretraining dataset sizes. The gains persist for both frozen and fine-tuned encoders, motivating predictive self-supervision in future large-scale particle-physics foundation models.

item.title: Update on transverse-spin azimuthal asymmetries in single-hadron SIDIS on transversely polarised deuterons at COMPASS (Artur Hoghmrtsyan (on behalf of the COMPASS Collaboration))
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Over the years, the COMPASS experiment at CERN has pursued an extensive SIDIS programme aimed at a comprehensive understanding of the structure of the nucleon, using a high-energy muon beam and polarised targets. Within this programme, measurements with a transversely polarised deuteron target were performed in 2022 using the 160 GeV/c muon beam. In single-hadron SIDIS on such a target, eight transverse-spin-dependent azimuthal asymmetries arise, providing sensitivity to several transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions and to subleading-twist partonic correlations. We report the simultaneous extraction of all eight asymmetries from the complete 2022 deuteron sample. The Collins and Sivers asymmetries, previously presented using about 70% of the 2022 statistics, are updated with the full sample and found consistent with the earlier result, while the six remaining asymmetries are presented for the first time with the full 2022 statistics. Combined with the existing proton results, these measurements complete a comprehensive COMPASS programme on transverse-spin effects in SIDIS, providing essential input for global analyses.

item.title: Prospects for exploring quantum-correlated neutral DD decays at STCF
item.dc:creator: Ying-Hao Wang et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We investigate the prospects for determining charm mixing, indirect CP violation and hadronic parameters in charm decays with quantum-correlated neutral charm mesons at the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility. The study is based on time-integrated double tag rates of coherent DD pairs produced at √(s)=3.773 and 4.030 GeV, from e⁺e⁻→D⁽)D⁽) processes. Here, one D is tagged with the quasi flavour-specific decays D→K⁻π⁺π⁺π⁻, K⁻π⁺π⁰, and K⁻π⁺, while the other D is detected with the final states in flavour-specific mode, CP eigenstate mode, or self-conjugate mode. The expected sensitivities are evaluated assuming an integrated luminosity of 1 ab⁻¹ at each energy point, demonstrating the capability on precise determination of the charm mixing parameters, the indirect CP violation parameters, the strong-phase differences, and the coherence factors. The constraints of the hadronic-parameters provide unique inputs to the CKM angle γ fit, while the measurements of charm mixing and indirect CP violation parameters are complementary to the time-dependent measurements in the Belle II and LHCb experiments.

item.title: Antenna-coupled microstrip summing network for wave-like dark matter searches
item.dc:creator: Chelsea Bartram et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A commonly used technology for axion and other wave-like dark matter searches is a microwave resonator. In such experiments, the detected signal strength depends on the coupling between the resonator and the microwave transmission line that delivers power to the amplifier. In Axion Dark Matter eXperiment (ADMX) and other cavity searches, this coupling is typically achieved using a compact wire antenna inserted into the cavity. While this approach is adequate for right-cylindrical cavities, it can become difficult to efficiently extract power from large-volume, multi-wavelength (V ≫λ³) resonators targeted for higher frequencies, such as those designed by ADMX-VERA (Volume Enhanced Resonant Axion). Here, we present a solution based on a microwave slot-antenna array capacitively coupled to a microstrip “summing network,” which coherently combines signals from multiple transmission lines into a single output. This summing architecture is adapted from designs originally developed for cosmic microwave background (CMB) detectors. We demonstrate the design and characterization of a new high-frequency resonator that employs this readout scheme in the 19-21 GHz range. Finally we discuss the potential to reach Dine-Fischler-Srednicki-Zhitnitsky (DFSZ) sensitivity using multiple summing network cavities fitted into a large volume.

item.title: Search for e⁺e⁻ →π⁰ K⁺K⁻J/ψ at √(s)= 4.26 ∼ 4.95 GeV
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using e⁺e⁻ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at 27 center-of-mass energies between 4.26 and 4.95 GeV corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 13.0 fb⁻¹, we report the first search for the process e⁺e⁻ →π⁰ K⁺K⁻J/ψ. We additionally probe the cross section spectra for potential charmonium-like vector states and invariant mass distributions for intermediate Z_c/Z_cs state signals, and find no resonant structures consistent with these exotic candidates. Given the absence of observed resonant signals, upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are determined for the Born cross sections, along with their best-fit values, as well as for the production of the intermediate states.

item.title: Improved measurement of ψ(3686)→π⁺π⁻ η
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using a sample of (2712.4 ±14.3) ×10⁶ ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector, we perform a partial wave analysis of the decay ψ(3686)→π⁺π⁻η with the π⁺π⁻ invariant mass in the ρ(770)⁰ mass region, [0.3, 2.2] GeV/c². The cross section line-shape around the ψ(3686) resonance is measured using energy-scan data sets, enabling the estimation of continuum contribution and its interference with the ψ(3686) resonance. The branching fraction of ψ(3686)→ρ(770)⁰η is determined to be (1.34 ±0.03±0.13) ×10⁻⁵. The ψ(3686)→a_2(1320)^±π^∓ decay is observed for the first time with a significance of 35.7σ, and its partial branching fraction is measured to be (2.13 ±0.05±0.32) ×10⁻⁵. The η-η^’ pseudoscalar mixing angle θ_P is then found to be (-11.2 ±1.6±3.6)^∘ or (-19.4±3.1±5.7)^∘, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic.

item.title: Precision measurement of the J/ψ→μ⁺μ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ branching fraction and search for a new gauge boson Z^' at BESIII
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present a precision measurement of the branching fraction of the rare decay J/ψ→μ⁺μ⁻μ⁺μ⁻, and a search for a new gauge boson Z^’ that couples only to the second and third lepton generations, using a data sample of (8998 ±39) ×10⁶ J/ψ events collected by the BESIII detector. The branching fraction of the J/ψ→μ⁺μ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ decay is measured to be B(J/ψ→μ⁺μ⁻μ⁺μ⁻⁾⁼[0.91±0.04 (stat.)±0.07 (syst.)]×10⁻⁶, representing the most precise measurement to date and consistent with the theoretical prediction within one standard deviation. Additionally, we search for CP asymmetry in the J/ψ→μ⁺μ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ decay and determine the T-odd observable to be A_T = [0.05±0.04 (stat.)±0.01 (syst.)], which is consistent with CP conservation. In the search for J/ψ→Z^’μ⁺μ⁻ via Z^’→μ⁺μ⁻, no significant Z^’ signal is observed in the μ⁺μ⁻ invariant mass region of (0.212, 2.6)~GeV/c², and we set upper limits on the U(1)_L_μ-L_τ model coupling constant g^’ ranging from 0.001 to 0.294 at the 90\% confidence level, which is comparable to the upper limits set by Belle II for Z^’ masses below 0.7~GeV/c².

item.title: High significance measurement of reactor coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering on germanium by CONUS+ (N. Ackermann (CONUS+ Collaboration) et al.)
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We report the most precise measurement to date of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEνNS) from reactor antineutrinos using the CONUS+ high-purity germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant. With an exposure of 1296 kg·days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis yields 1555 ±152 CEνNS events, with a significance of 10.2 σ, in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of 1701 ±198 events within 0.6 standard deviations. The result also determines the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV, sin²θ_W = 0.225 ±0.022, consistent with the Standard Model prediction.

item.title: Analysis of CONUS+ run 2: Detector performance, background model and CEνNS measurement (N. Ackermann (CONUS+ Collaboration) et al.)
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEνNS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CEνNS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. Following a detector upgrade that replaced three of the original 1 kg high-purity germanium detectors with larger 2.42 kg diodes, this paper presents the analysis of the CONUS+ run 2 dataset, including the detector characterization, the background model, the signal prediction and expected sensitivity, and the extraction of the CEνNS signal. The new detectors reach a background level per unit mass reduced by approximately a factor of two relative to the original detectors, while reaching energy thresholds between 140 and 170 eV_ee. With an exposure of 1296 kg·days reactor-on and 86 kg·days reactor-off, a blind likelihood analysis fitting directly the number of signal counts yields N_s = 1555 ±152 CEνNS events, corresponding to a significance of 10.2σ. The result is in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of 1701 ±198 events, with N_s/N_SM = 0.91 ±0.14.

item.title: Observation of χ_c1,2→p K⁻ K⁻ Ξ̅⁺ +c.c. and search for χ_c0→p K⁻ K⁻ Ξ̅⁺ +c.c.
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

By analyzing (2.712±0.014)×10⁹ ψ(3686) events collected by the BESIII detector, we report the first experimental study of the decays χ_cJ→p K⁻ K⁻ Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c. (J=0,1,2). The decays χ_c1→p K⁻ K⁻ Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c. and χ_c2→p K⁻ K⁻ Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c. are observed for the first time with significances of 9.0σ each, and their branching fractions are determined to be ℬ_χ_c1→p K⁻ K⁻ Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c. =(9.6⁺².2_-2.0±0.8)×10⁻⁶, and ℬ_χ_c2→p K⁻ K⁻ Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c. =(7.5⁺¹.8_-1.5±0.5)×10⁻⁶, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. No significant signal is observed for χ_c0→p K⁻ K⁻ Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c., and an upper limit on its branching fraction of 12.7×10⁻⁶ is established at the 90\% confidence level.

item.title: Search for Neutrino-Produced Long-Lived Particles Using the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger Beam Telescope
item.dc:creator: R. Acciarri et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) is a liquid argon time projection chamber in Fermilab’s Short-Baseline Neutrino Program, positioned 110 meters from the neutrino target along the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB). In addition to its neutrino physics goals, SBND enables searches for new physics, including long-lived particles (LLPs) produced via neutrino-nucleus upscattering that decay into visible final states. Although neutrino data taking with the full SBND experiment began in December 2024, a subset of the Cosmic Ray Tagger (CRT) system operated from 2017–2018 as a standalone detector, referred to as the CRT Beam Telescope, collecting data corresponding to 2.95×10²⁰ protons on target from the BNB. Originally intended for commissioning and performance studies, the substantial dataset collected also enables searches for displaced LLP decays. This paper presents the first search for physics beyond the Standard Model using data from the SBND CRT Beam Telescope, targeting LLP decays into electron-positron pairs. We observe no significant excess above the expected background and set 90% confidence-level upper limits on an effective production cross section at the level of 10⁻³⁸ cm² for laboratory decay lengths of 0.3-100 m. These results complement existing searches by probing displaced decay signatures at meter-scale decay lengths.

item.title: Search for nonresonant production of strongly coupled dark matter in proton-proton collisions at √(s) = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A search is presented for semivisible jets produced in nonresonant processes, using proton-proton collision data at √(s) = 13 TeV, collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb⁻¹. These jets, containing both visible and invisible particles, would indicate the presence of dark matter arising from a strongly coupled hidden sector. The signal model includes a bifundamental scalar that couples simultaneously to standard model quarks and dark-sector quarks, the latter forming semivisible jets. The final state therefore includes missing transverse momentum aligned with a jet, rather than recoiling against standard model particles as typically required by conventional collider dark-matter searches. Two separate machine-learning strategies are employed to identify semivisible jets: a supervised graph neural network and an unsupervised autoencoder. No significant excess corresponding to dark-sector signal hypotheses is observed. Upper limits at 95% confidence level on the signal production cross section are determined for each strategy and interpreted as exclusions in the signal model parameter space. The supervised search excludes mediator masses between 0.5 and 2.4 TeV, depending on the other signal model parameters. For signal models with semivisible jets containing higher fractions of stable dark-matter particles, the unsupervised search demonstrates increased sensitivity with 5 (11)% higher expected (observed) mediator mass exclusions than the supervised search.

item.title: Search for the rare decay η^'→3γ
item.dc:creator: M. Ablikim et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using a data sample of (10087 ±44) ×10⁶ J/ψ events collected with the BESIII detector, we search for the rare decay η^’→3γ via the process J/ψ→γη^’. No significant signal is observed and an upper limit on the branching fraction of η^’→3γ is set at ℬ(η^’→3γ) < 2.25×10⁻⁵ at the 90\% confidence level. This result improves the previous upper limit by more than a factor of four.

item.title: MATHUSLA: A Proposed Long-Lived Particle Detector for High-Luminosity LHC (Miriam Diamond
item.dc:creator: Department of Physics et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Beyond the Standard Model long-lived particles (LLPs) appear in many theories that address fundamental open questions, such as the hierarchy problem and the nature of dark matter. The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) may be producing copious numbers of neutral LLPs with masses above a GeV, only for these sneaky particles to escape the main detectors without being spotted. To fill this gap, we have proposed MATHUSLA (MAssive Timing Hodoscope for Ultra-Stable neutraL pArticles), which would be constructed on the surface above CMS and would take data during High-Luminosity LHC operations. The detector would be composed of several layers of solid plastic scintillator threaded with wavelength-shifting fibers that connect to silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs), and would monitor an empty, air-filled decay volume. The Conceptual Design Report (CDR) published in 2025 sets out a benchmark geometry of 40m x 40m x 16m, with a modular detector construction scheme that would allow data collection to begin as soon as the first module is installed. This proceeding documents the results of more detailed studies conducted since the CDR on the detector’s potential location, mechanical engineering of modules, data acquisition system, cosmic ray backgrounds, event selection criteria, and trigger algorithms.

item.title: First measurement of ψ(3686)→p̅ K⁺ Σ^*(1385)⁰ + c.c. and ψ(3686)→p̅ K^*(892)⁰ Σ⁺ + c.c.
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Based on a sample of (2712.4 ±14.3) ×10⁶ ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, we report the first observation of the decays ψ(3686)→p̅ K⁺ Σ^(1385)⁰⁺c.c. and ψ(3686)→p̅ K^(892)⁰ Σ⁺ + c.c.. The corresponding branching fractions are determined to be ℬ(ψ(3686)→p̅K⁺Σ^(1385)⁰⁺c.c.)=(3.94±0.15_stat.±0.24_syst.)×10⁻⁵ and ℬ(ψ(3686)→p̅K^(892)⁰Σ⁺⁺c.c.)=(4.93±0.14_stat.±0.30_syst.)×10⁻⁵. Furthermore, we search for the hidden-strange pentaquark candidates N_x(1875) and N_x(2100) in the invariant mass spectra of K⁺ Σ^(1385)⁰ and K^(892)⁰ Σ⁺, respectively. No significant signals are observed and the upper limits on the branching fractions at the 90% confidence level are ℬ(ψ(3686)→p̅N_x(1875)→p̅K⁺Σ^(1385)⁰⁾<1.58×10⁻⁶ and ℬ(ψ(3686)→p̅N_x(2100)→p̅K^(892)⁰Σ⁺⁾<3.09×10⁻⁷.

item.title: LHμC: A high energy, high luminosity muon-hadron collider at CERN
item.dc:creator: Krzysztof Piotrzkowski
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The latest developments regarding the feasibility of muon-hadron collisions, achieved through the major reuse of LHeC infrastructure, are presented - at the LHμC, a 1 or 2 TeV μ⁺ beam collides with a 7 TeV proton beam, resulting in the μ⁺p centre-of-mass energy of 5.3 or 7.5 TeV, respectively, at an average luminosity close to 10³⁴cm⁻²s⁻¹. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including exceptional prospects for neutrino science, and is followed by a presentation of the LHμC concept in a nutshell - from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations regarding the machine-detector interface and the general-purpose detector are also presented. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying unique and powerful synergies between the LHμC, LHeC, FCC and Muon Collider projects.

item.title: Observation of the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ state in B⁰→D^*-D⁰K⁺ decays
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A study of resonant structures in B⁰ →D^-D⁰K⁺ decays is presented. The analysis uses proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment at center-of-mass energies of √(s) = 7, 8, and 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 9 fb⁻¹. The analysis demonstrates that the existing known excited D_s⁺ resonances in the D⁰K⁺ spectrum are insufficient to describe the data. The inclusion of the tetraquark state T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ improves the description of the data with a statistical significance exceeding 5σ. This corresponds to the first observation of the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ →D^- D⁰ decay. The measured properties of the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ state are consistent with those previously measured in its decay to the ψ(2S)π⁻ final state.

item.title: Prediction of the Geoneutrino Signal at the Jinping Neutrino Experiment
item.dc:creator: Kaikai Meng et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present refined predictions of the geoneutrino flux for the 500-tonne Jinping Neutrino Experiment (JNE). We construct a local crustal model with a resolution of \(0.2^\circ\times0.2^\circ\) based on the SWChinaCVM-2.0 seismic velocity model and integrate it with CRUST1.0 to establish our reference model. For comparison, we also calculate the geoneutrino flux using ECM1 and CRUST1.0 as standalone global crustal models. Assuming an energy scale of 500~p.e./MeV and an exposure of 500~t×1500~days, we predict the inverse beta decay event spectrum, including both the geoneutrino signal and the reactor antineutrino background. The distinct spectral shapes of the ²³⁸U, ²³²Th, and reactor antineutrino components allow their respective contributions to be obtained through spectral fitting. These predictions provide inputs for the JNE data analysis, particularly for extracting the mantle geoneutrino signal and testing competing bulk silicate Earth models.

item.title: Natural Chlorine Enhances Antineutrino Detection in the Deep Ocean
item.dc:creator: Ruike Cao et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Large-volume neutrino telescopes such as IceCube and KM3NeT exploit natural ice or water as detection media, but their sparse instrumentation makes MeV neutrino interactions difficult to identify individually. We show that chlorine naturally abundant in seawater provides an intrinsic neutron-capture target that enables efficient tagging of electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay. In contrast to the 2.2 MeV γ-ray from neutron capture on hydrogen, capture on chlorine produces an ∼8.6 MeV γ-ray cascade on a shorter time scale, yielding a distinctive delayed-coincidence signature. Using measured seawater properties at the TRIDENT site and a detector-level simulation, we find that chlorine-assisted tagging can extend the core-collapse supernova 5σ discovery reach from ∼50 to over 100 kpc. We validate the underlying detection principle with a salted-water experiment at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory, observing correlated neutron-capture signatures under suppressed cosmic muon background conditions. Natural seawater thus transforms the deep ocean into an intrinsically enhanced antineutrino detection medium, opening new opportunities for MeV neutrino astronomy and distributed measurements of reactor and geophysical antineutrinos.

item.title: CURTAIN: Towards a Foundation Model for Neutrino Telescopes
item.dc:creator: Severin Magel et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Neutrino telescopes record more than a trillion photon detections per year, yet there does not exist a self-supervised learning (SSL) task which fully satisfies all three conditions: improving as the pretraining set grows, transferring to a different detector, and outperforming the best model trained without pretraining at all. We introduce CURTAIN, a temporal masking scheme and the first SSL task for neutrino telescopes that achieves all of these goals. Downstream performance monotonically improves with the number of pretraining events, as predicted by scaling laws. Our encoder builds on DeepIce, currently the leading model on the NuBench benchmarks direction reconstruction task. Pretraining it with CURTAIN reduces its median angular error by 45% and its median energy error by 31% compared to training from scratch. It also transfers to a detector geometry never seen in pretraining, reducing the median angular error by 36% compared to training from scratch. At matched capacity and pretraining data, CURTAIN-pretrained encoders beat those pretrained by existing SSL tasks on both tasks and at every pretraining set size.

item.title: Precise Measurement of the Inclusive Cross Sections of Open-Charm Mesons at Energies from 3.80 to 4.95 GeV
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using e⁺e⁻ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies from 3.80 to 4.95 GeV, the inclusive production cross sections of open-charm mesons, σ(e⁺e⁻→D⁰/D⁺/D_s⁺⁺X), are measured by tagging a D⁰, D⁺, or D_s⁺ meson, where X denotes any accompanying particles. Open-charm production dominates the total hadronic yield above threshold. Therefore these measurements provide a vital reference for understanding hadron production and for validating global R value results. The results offer crucial inputs for investigating heavier charmonia and exotic states coupled to open-charm final states, while serving as a benchmark for comparison with the sum of measured exclusive channels. This comparison directly evaluates the completeness of current exclusive datasets and clarifies the underlying hadronization mechanisms in the open-charm region.

item.title: Measurements of the branching fractions of Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺ π⁰ and Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺ η decays at Belle and Belle II
item.dc:creator: Belle et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present a study of the three-body, singly Cabibbo-suppressed decays Λ_c⁺ →ΛK⁺ π⁰ and Λ_c⁺ →ΛK⁺ η using data recorded with the Belle and Belle II detectors at the KEKB and SuperKEKB e⁺ e⁻ colliders. The data samples correspond to integrated luminosities of 980fb⁻¹ and 570fb⁻¹, respectively. We measure their branching-fraction ratios relative to the Cabibbo-favored decay Λ_c⁺ →Λπ⁺ π⁰ as ℬ(Λ_c⁺ →ΛK⁺ π⁰⁾/ℬ(Λ_c⁺ →Λπ⁺ π⁰⁾⁼⁽¹.82 ±0.07 ±0.07)%, with significantly improved precision compared to the previous measurement, and ℬ(Λ_c⁺ →ΛK⁺ η)/ℬ(Λ_c⁺ →Λπ⁺ π⁰⁾⁼⁽⁸.73 ±0.35 ±0.43)×10⁻³, corresponding to the first observation of the Λ_c⁺ →ΛK⁺ η decay with a statistical significance exceeding 10 standard deviations. The first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. Using the world-average value of the branching fraction for Λ_c⁺ →Λπ⁺ π⁰, we obtain the branching fractions ℬ(Λ_c⁺ →ΛK⁺ π⁰⁾⁼⁽¹.29±0.05±0.05±0.06)×10⁻³ and ℬ(Λ_c⁺ →ΛK⁺ η)=(6.20±0.25±0.31±0.30)×10⁻⁴, where the third uncertainty arises from the uncertainty in the world-average value of ℬ(Λ_c⁺ →Λπ⁺ π⁰⁾. The measured ℬ(Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺η) is significantly larger than predictions based on SU(3) flavor symmetry.

item.title: A superconducting LC resonator in a multi-tesla magnetic field for tabletop kHz gravitational-wave detection
item.dc:creator: D. Ahn et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present a concept for a superconducting inductance–capacitance (LC) resonator immersed in a magnetic field for gravitational-wave detection in the kHz band. In the long-wavelength limit, a gravitational wave in a static magnetic field induces an oscillating magnetic-field perturbation proportional to the static magnetic field applied to the resonator and to the gravitational-wave strain. We show that a superconducting pickup circuit can convert this perturbation into a flux signal read out by a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID)-based or quantum-limited amplifier chain. Inspired by resonant-mass detectors, we develop a three-loop coupled-circuit model and derive the equivalent strain-noise spectrum, including thermal noise, SQUID backaction, and measurement imprecision. Prototype measurements demonstrate a quality factor of Q≃5×10⁵, while Q=10⁷ is considered as a future development target. Under the assumed flux coupling and an idealized quantum-limited SQUID noise model, optimized circuits yield projected strain sensitivities of order 10⁻²¹ Hz⁻¹/2 over 100 Hz bands in the 1–20 kHz range. Increasing the active high-field volume and improving quantum-limited readout could enable further sensitivity gains. This compact, tunable detector concept could complement interferometric gravitational-wave searches and motivate investigations of high-frequency astrophysical sources.

item.title: Cross Section Measurements and Searches for New Structures in e⁺e⁻ Annihilations at BESIII
item.dc:creator: Hao Liu
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The BESIII collaboration has collected large data samples in the center-of-mass energy range from 1.84 to 4.95 GeV. These data provide a low-background environment and wide energy range for studying the cross sections and the spectroscopy of charmonia. In this article, we review the recent achievements by the BESIII collaboration, including for searching new structures of XYZ particles and the hyperonic production over open-charm threshold.

item.title: Study of Λ CP Asymmetry Parameter and Electric Dipole Moment at the Super Tau-Charm Facility
item.dc:creator: Mingyu Yu et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Searching for new mechanisms of CP violation beyond the Standard Model is essential to explain the observed matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe. By analyzing the full angular distribution of the quantum-entangled ΛΛ̅ pairs from J/ψ decays, the preliminary sensitivity of CP asymmetry parameter A_CP and Electric Dipole Moment of Λ is studied at the future Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF). Based on 3.4 ×10¹² J/ψ events at STCF, the projected sensitivity for A_CP^Λ reaches the 10⁻⁴ level, while the Λ EDM can be probed at 10⁻²⁰ e cm. These results highly indicate that STCF will provide an unprecedented opportunity to search for new mechanisms of CP violation with an expected world-leading precision.

item.title: The Electron-Recoil Response Tail and the LZ High-Energy Event Background
item.dc:creator: Triparno Bandyopadhyay et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We reconstruct the continuum electron-recoil contribution to the LZ background expectation from the collaboration’s released simulation configuration. The released model specifies a definite response tail, but the published calibration information supplies no bound on how far the physical tail may depart from it at the probabilities the expectation depends on. Distributions reproducing the executable model’s mean, variance, and standardised skewness exactly, and its event-conditioned 10, 50, and 90\% \(N_e\) quantiles to about one per cent, differ in the relevant tail probability by more than five orders of magnitude. The ladder is short: a tail agreeing with that central characterisation to 0.14\% in the quantiles lifts the electron-recoil contribution out of the negligible range, and one agreeing to 0.47\% makes it comparable to the entire background quoted for the comparison region. We go on to identify the measurements that would settle it.

item.title: Pretraining on boosted boson decays for polarization tagging of hadronic W bosons
item.dc:creator: Saptaparna Bhattacharya
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Longitudinally polarized weak bosons probe the unitarization of vector-boson scattering. At large boosts, longitudinal and transverse W bosons produce jets with the same mass and two-prong structure, distinguished only by the decay angle. Longitudinal bosons are rare: they occur in only 0.3% of W+jet events at these large boosts. We ask where the polarization information of a boosted W boson lies and how much a tagger can recover. Requiring both decay quarks within the jet truncates the decay-angle distribution at an edge set by m/(p_T R), which we show bounds any hadronic polarization tagger. Within this acceptance, the decay angle carries essentially all the polarization information of a jet in W+jet events. Polarized samples are costly to simulate for vector-boson scattering, so we pretrain a point-edge transformer on 10⁷ unpolarized jets of boosted bosons, top quarks and QCD and test how much it recovers from few labels. Fine-tuned on 783 labeled jets per class with its transformer blocks kept fixed, the network pretrained to classify these jets improves on training from scratch, but generic pretraining on a broad mix of jets and a boosted decision tree on substructure observables do as well. The best taggers recover most, but not all, of the separation the decay angle allows, and student networks with a few hundred times fewer parameters, trained by knowledge distillation, match their teacher. More information lies outside the jet. The production angle, reconstructed with the recoiling jet, improves every tagger. In diboson production and vector-boson scattering at matrix-element level, the production kinematics carry more information than the decay angles of both bosons. Trading the generality of a jet tagger for an event-level tagger trained on the process thus brings significant gains, which measurements of longitudinal vector-boson scattering could exploit.

item.title: Charmed baryon decays at BESIII
item.dc:creator: Chengzhi He
item.description:
