New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

BESIII has accumulated 6.4~fb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ collision data at center-of-mass energies from 4.60 to 4.95~GeV, corresponding to the world’s largest sample of Λ_c⁺Λ̅_c⁻ pairs. This proceeding summarizes recent BESIII results on charmed baryon decays, including the first observation of the transverse polarization of the Λ_c⁺ in e⁺e⁻→Λ_c⁺Λ̅_c⁻, a precision measurement of the inclusive decay Λ_c⁺→ΛX, the first observations of Λ_c⁺→ne⁺ν_e and Λ_c⁺→nπ⁺η with deep-learning techniques, the first observation of Λ_c⁺→pK⁻e⁺ν_e together with evidence for Λ_c⁺→Σ^±π^∓e⁺ν_e, and partial wave analyses of Λ_c⁺→Λπ⁺η.

item.title: Open Science with the LHCb Ntupling Service (Christine A. Aidala
item.dc:creator: University of Michigan et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The data samples collected at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN are highly valuable, and the analysis of these data has led to numerous discoveries and the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. Preserving and providing open access to these data for future analysts is imperative to maximize the scientific output of the collected data. The LHCb collaboration has developed a novel approach to this pursuit of open science, the LHCb Ntupling Service: a web service for on-demand production and publishing of custom LHCb open data, providing open access to both Run 1, and for the first time, Run 2 proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment, amounting to over 4 PB of data to explore.

item.title: Light meson decays at BESIII
item.dc:creator: Kailu Li
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The world’s largest sample of J/ψ events accumulated with the BESIII detector offers a unique opportunity to investigate η and η’ physics via the radiative transition processes J/ψ→γη/η’. A selection of recent highlights in light meson spectroscopy achieved at BESIII is reviewed in these proceedings, including evidence for the cusp effect in η’ →π⁰π⁰η, precision studies of the decay mechanisms of η→3π and η’ →4π, electromagnetic transition form factor measurements with η/η’ →γe⁺e⁻ and η’ →π⁺π⁻l⁺l⁻, as well as searches for rare decays of η and η’ into lepton pairs, including η→l⁺l⁻ and η/η’ →l⁺l⁻l⁺l⁻~(l = e, μ).

item.title: ceci n'est pas un tagger, can an LLM flavour-tag a jet?
item.dc:creator: Andrea Coccaro et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly capable of reasoning about scientific problems, effectively mastering and synthesizing entire fields of research and providing, for the first time, access to a distilled and queryable form of scientific knowledge. As the integration of LLMs rapidly spreads across the large collaborations of high-energy physics, aiming to re-think and optimize analysis workflows, it remains unclear whether the knowledge acquired during pretraining can support quantitative inference on physical data. Moving beyond the applications currently pursued by the community, we pose a simple question: can an LLM classify the flavour of a hadronic jet? An LLM is therefore asked to assign flavour probabilities (b, c, light, τ) to jets from a public ATLAS flavour-tagging sample, using only reconstructed constituents. Under a small set of constraints, the model is not allowed to write code or implement conventional algorithms and must instead perform the inference directly from its pretrained knowledge and the available inputs. We report two complementary results and make publicly available, through a GitHub repository, all the code required to reproduce the experiment and obtain the quantitative results presented in this work. First, the model achieves non-trivial discrimination between flavours, which we compare with recent ATLAS flavour-tagging algorithms. Second, the model accompanies each prediction with a natural language rationale. The physical concepts invoked in these rationales correlate with the truth flavour and reproduce the features traditionally associated with each jet category. Flavour tagging thus provides a laboratory for broader questions: how can we actively leverage the corpus of scientific knowledge accumulated over decades of research? Could LLMs serve as a general source of scientific context for task-specific algorithms?

item.title: Search for new physics with charm data at BESIII (Xinyu Chai (on behalf of the BESIII Collaboration))
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Up to now, the Standard Model (SM) remains confronted with several outstanding issues, including the matter-antimatter asymmetry in the universe, as well as the masses, oscillations, and hierarchical structure of neutrinos. These challenges are closely tied to the naturalness and stability of the SM, and have motivated numerous proposals for new physics beyond the SM. The BESIII experiment has accumulated the world’s largest data samples at the J/ψ and ψ(3686) resonances, providing an ideal environment for probing signatures of physics beyond the SM. This proceeding presents a summary of recent results published by the BESIII Collaboration on the searches for lepton/baryon number violation (LNV/BNV), charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV), and charmonium weak decays.

item.title: Low-Latency Beam-Background Suppression for the BESIII Trigger System Using Machine Learning Trained on Experimental Data
item.dc:creator: Hanlin Zhang et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Beam-induced backgrounds contribute to the trigger and data-acquisition rate at high-luminosity electron-positron colliders. Their dependence on beam and machine conditions motivates data-driven studies alongside simulation. A data-driven machine-learning method for trigger-level beam-background suppression is developed using experimental data recorded by BESIII. Compact neural-network classifiers are trained and evaluated for two trigger configurations: one based only on tracking and time-of-flight information, and one based only on electromagnetic-calorimeter information. Each classifier uses 48 binary Level-1 trigger conditions of the BESIII detector. The models distinguish hadron events from beam-background events and are evaluated against the established trigger selection at matched hadron-event efficiency. Relative to the established trigger selection, the beam-background false-positive rate is reduced by 20-60% across the studied configurations and center-of-mass energies, with stable suppression performance as tested using random-trigger data. Hardware-oriented synthesis indicates that the compact network is suitable for low-latency FPGA implementation. The proposed method can reduce the fraction of beam-background events in the trigger stream in future BESIII trigger upgrades. It also provides a reference for trigger optimization at future high-luminosity electron-positron colliders.

item.title: Measurements of time-dependent b-hadron properties in LHCb
item.dc:creator: Lucas Foreman
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

These proceedings present the latest measurements of time-dependent properties of b-hadrons using the LHCb Run 2 data set. Three results are presented. The first of these is a measurement of the CKM phase ϕ_s with B_s⁰→J/ψπ⁺π⁻. This result improves the determination in this channel, obtaining a result of ϕ_s = -77±34(stat)±7(syst) mrad. This result is included in the LHCb global average to obtain ϕ_s = -41±17 mrad. Additionally, a determination of the penguin contributions, Δϕ_s, to measurements of ϕ_s using B⁰→J/ψρ⁰⁽⁷⁷⁰⁾ is presented. This measurement constitutes the first observation of CP-violation in B_0 →J/ψρ⁰⁽⁷⁷⁰⁾ decays. The CKM phase 2β is measured and is determined to be 2β^eff_ccd = 0.710±0.084±0.051 rad. The most stringent constraint on penguin contributions is obtained and determined to be Δϕ_s = 5.0±4.6 mrad. Finally, the first measurement of time-dependent CP-violation in a b→s l⁺ l⁻ process using the decay B_s⁰ →K_S μ⁺ μ⁻ is presented. The time-dependent coefficients of this decay are determined to be C=-0.13±0.32(stat)±0.04(syst) and S=+0.82±0.29(stat)±0.05(syst).

item.title: Neural Bayesian Online Calibration with Deficient Simulators for MADMAX Dark Matter Experiment
item.dc:creator: Nabil Salama
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Scientific experiments often rely on deficient simulators and hardware whose commanded settings differ from the states realized in practice, limiting reliable optimization and inference. A Bayesian online calibration framework is introduced for experiments with at least one directly measurable simulator output and potentially latent quantities of scientific interest. Pre-calibration data are used to learn state-dependent effective simulator parameters, while a normalizing flow enables amortized posterior inference from measurement histories. During calibration, measurement and positioning uncertainties are propagated, and hardware commands are selected by balancing expected improvement with information gain. The framework is applied to the MADMAX dark matter experiment, where measured reflectivity is used to calibrate a deficient disk-booster simulator and infer the unobservable axion-signal power boost factor. Experimental validation on the MADMAX experiment is ongoing.

item.title: Measurement of the relative phase between the strong and electromagnetic amplitudes in J/ψ→Σ⁺ Σ̅⁻
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using 284 pb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies between 3.00 and 3.12 GeV, the relative phase between the strong and electromagnetic interaction amplitudes in the process J/ψ→Σ⁺ Σ̅⁻ is determined. The relative phase is measured to be (107.9 ±24.9)^∘ or (-107.6 ±24.3)^∘, where the uncertainty includes both statistical and systematic sources. This is the first experimental determination of the strong-electromagnetic phase difference in J/ψ decays to a hyperon-antihyperon pair. The branching fraction ℬ_J/ψ→Σ⁺ Σ̅⁻ is measured to be (1.14 ±0.04)×10⁻³ for the positive phase solution or (1.19 ±0.04) ×10⁻³ for the negative phase solution. These results provide important input for testing perturbative QCD predictions and studies of SU(3) flavor symmetry.

item.title: Observation of the Ξ_b⁻→Ξ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ and study of the Ξ_b⁻→Ξ⁻ψ(2S) decays
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The rare decay Ξ_b⁻→Ξ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ is observed for the first time using proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment at centre-of-mass energies of 7, 8 and~13 TeV, corresponding to integrated luminosities of 1, 2 and 6 fb⁻¹, respectively. Its branching fraction is reported in intervals of the dimuon invariant mass squared. The integrated value of B(Ξ_b⁻→Ξ⁻μ⁺μ⁻⁾ is measured to be (118 ±24 ±7 ±38 ) ×10⁻⁸, where the first uncertainty is statistical, the second is systematic and the third uncertainty arises from the normalisation branching fraction B(Ξ_b⁻→Ξ⁻J/ψ), whose uncertainty is dominated by SU(3)-breaking effects. In addition, the ratio of the branching fractions of the Ξ_b⁻→Ξ⁻ψ(2S) and the Ξ_b⁻→Ξ⁻J/ψ decays is measured to be 0.491 ±0.041 ±0.019.

item.title: A comparative study of variational quantum classifiers and classical machine learning for tW-tt̅ discrimination at the LHC
item.dc:creator: Rohan Hindocha et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Precise measurements of single top-quark production in the associated tW-channel require efficient discrimination against the dominant tt̅ background. In this work, we investigate the applicability of quantum machine learning to this classification problem using the Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) algorithm. Simulated proton-proton collision events from CMS Open Data corresponding to Run-2 are employed to train and evaluate the VQC model. Its performance is compared with two established classical approaches, Boosted Decision Trees (BDTs) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) using both machine learning metrics and physics-motivated metrics that describe the Signal Significance as a function of Signal Efficiency. The comparison is performed separately for the dileptonic e-μ channel and for the resolved and boosted hadronic topologies. In addition, signal-enriched and background-enriched phase-space regions are studied to assess the dependence of classifier performance on event topology. Our results provide a systematic benchmark for the application of VQC for a realistic High Energy Physics classification task and identify the analysis regimes wherein quantum-inspired models offer competitive discrimination with respect to established classical techniques.

item.title: Laboratory Characterization of a Ge-CCD Prototype for Future Near-Infrared Astronomical Instrumentation
item.dc:creator: Emi Tamura et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Germanium charge-coupled devices (Ge-CCDs) extend CCD imaging beyond the silicon cutoff and are candidate detectors for the near-infrared channel of future astronomical instruments, in particular the spectrographs of next-generation wide-field surveys. We report the laboratory characterization at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) of a prototype fabricated at MIT Lincoln Laboratory. We describe the cryogenic test system and readout, and present measurements of the output waveform, dark current, readout noise, and X-ray response. The dark current at 94.69 K is 26.12 ±0.08 e⁻ pixel⁻¹ s⁻¹. Under ⁵⁵Fe irradiation without on-chip binning, the charge generated by an X-ray is confined within 2×2 pixels, and the Mn Kα line has a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 8.5 ±0.1% for single-pixel events. Since the charge generated by X-rays above about 30 keV spreads over 3×3 or more pixels, the CCD was operated with 2×2 on-chip binning at higher energies. This yielded FWHMs of 8.4±0.4% at 30.9 keV (¹³³Ba, ASCA grades 0, 2, 3, 4, and 6) and 7.45±0.04% at 59.5 keV (²⁴¹Am, all grades). These results establish a baseline for the device and for the BNL test system. Measurements of the temperature dependence, optical response, and charge-transfer performance will connect this baseline to the requirements of near-infrared astronomical instruments.

item.title: A REST-based Monte Carlo Simulation and Data Analysis Framework for the NνDEx Experiment
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Huang et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The NνDEx experiment is designed to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay (0νββ) of ⁸²Se and is planned to be deployed at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL). It employs a high-pressure time projection chamber (TPC) filled with ⁸²SeF_6 gas and a Topmetal pixelated charge readout system. The high Q_ββ value of ⁸²Se, together with the track reconstruction capability of a gaseous TPC, provides strong potential for background suppression. In this work, we develop a full simulation and reconstruction framework for the NνDEx experiment based on the REST (Rare Event Searches Toolkit) software framework. To meet the detector-specific requirements of NνDEx, customized simulation processes are implemented to describe the detector geometry, electron drift and diffusion, the Topmetal readout plane, signal formation, and electronics response. These developments enable a complete software description of the detector response from energy deposition to digitized waveforms. A waveform-fitting-based reconstruction method is further applied to the simulated signals to extract the deposited charge and reconstruct the event energy. For simulated signal events, the reconstructed energy resolution reaches a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of less than 1\%, satisfying the design requirement of the experiment. The resulting simulation and reconstruction chain provides a basis for future studies of detector response, background rejection, event classification, and optimization of the NνDEx detector design.

item.title: Reactor Antineutrino Detection with JUNO-TAO: Commissioning Performance and First Results
item.dc:creator: JUNO Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The Taishan Antineutrino Observatory (TAO) is a satellite experiment of JUNO, designed to measure the reactor antineutrino energy spectrum with high precision at a baseline of 43.2~m from a reactor core using a 2.8-ton spherical liquid-scintillator detector, 1.8~m in diameter, operated at -50 degree and instrumented with 4,024 silicon photomultiplier tiles. The TAO detector installation was completed in 2025, and physics data taking began on 10 February 2026. This paper reports the detector design, calibration strategy, and performance based on commissioning data and the first physics runs. Stable cryogenic operation has been achieved, and about 90\% of the readout channels are retained for physics analysis after channel-quality selections. The detector light yield is measured to be about 4000~photoelectrons/MeV after correction for dark noise and optical crosstalk, using neutron capture on hydrogen in inverse beta decay (IBD) events. The energy resolution is about 2.8\% for \(^{68}\)Ge at the detector center and about 3.7\% for \(^{137}\)Cs at \(R=193\)~mm. This energy-resolution performance is among the best reported for reactor-antineutrino detectors and enables TAO to measure the reactor antineutrino spectrum with high precision. Within the fiducial volume of \(R < 800\)~mm, the vertex reconstruction bias remains within \(\pm 30~\mathrm{mm}\), and the resolution is approximately \(70~\mathrm{mm}\) over most of the fiducial volume. The combined muon-tagging efficiency of the veto system is about 97\%. Using 31.3 days of reactor-on data and 29.4 days of reactor-off data, a significant excess of IBD candidates is observed in the reactor-on sample relative to the reactor-off sample, with candidate rates of 2900±10 events/day and 419±4 events/day, respectively. The results demonstrate that TAO has reached a high performance level in reactor antineutrino measurement.

item.title: Hyperon--nucleon interactions at BESIII
item.dc:creator: Hong-Fei Shen
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Hyperon–nucleon interactions provide essential information on the strange sector of baryon–baryon forces, with implications for hypernuclei, dense baryonic matter, and non-perturbative QCD. Direct experimental information, however, remains scarce because hyperons are short lived and intense conventional hyperon beams are difficult to produce. At BESIII, hyperons and antihyperons produced in charmonium decays can instead be used as incident particles, while the detector material serves as an effective fixed target. This approach has enabled a new program of hyperon–nucleon studies at an e⁺e⁻ collider. Representative results include the first study of Ξ⁰ⁿ→Ξ⁻p using Ξ⁰–nucleus scattering, measurements of elastic Λp→Λp and Λ̅p→Λ̅p scattering, and recent observations of Λ̅p annihilation into multi-meson final states. These measurements demonstrate that BESIII can operate as an effective hyperon–nucleon scattering facility and provide new experimental constraints on the poorly explored strange sector of baryon–baryon interactions.

item.title: First Observation of the Radiative Decay D⁰ →γω
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We report the first observation of the radiative charm decay D⁰ →γω with a significance of 6.0σ. The analysis uses 20.3\,fb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at a center-of-mass energy of 3.773\,GeV, and employs a deep learning strategy based on the Particle Transformer architecture. The absolute branching fraction of ℬ(D⁰→γω)=(2.12±0.40_stat±0.25_syst)×10⁻⁵ confirms the dominance of long-distance hadronic dynamics in radiative charm decays and provides a valuable benchmark for testing non-perturbative QCD calculations of D →γV transitions.

item.title: Achieving a 0.49 keV threshold in the COSINE-100 dark matter experiment (J. Kim (COSINE-100 Collaboration) et al.)
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The COSINE-100 experiment searched for weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) with NaI(Tl) crystals at the Yangyang Underground Laboratory. Using its full 6-year dataset, we lower the analysis threshold to 0.49 keV. A multi-layer perceptron classifier separates scintillation events from photomultiplier tube noise. It is trained with approximately 3×10⁶ simulated scintillation waveforms per crystal, separately for groups of events with similar numbers of photoelectron clusters. The selection keeps more than 10% of scintillation events at 0.49 keV while limiting noise contamination to below 1%. The selection efficiency is validated with ²²Na-calibration data and internal ²²Na events, and the selection performance is stable over the six years of data taking. With this threshold, the median expected upper limit on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section reaches 1.1×10⁻³⁶ cm² at a WIMP mass of 2.5 GeV/c², probing previously unexplored parameter space in the 2.0-2.8 GeV/c² mass range.

item.title: MoEDAL-MAPP: the first dedicated search experiment at the LHC
item.dc:creator: John R. Ellis et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

This special issue brings together a collection of original research articles and review papers addressing topics directly related to the MoEDAL-MAPP experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The experiment is designed to search for (meta-)stable, anomalously ionising particles predicted by theoretical extensions of the Standard Model. Several contributions explore the theoretical and phenomenological aspects of models of particular relevance to the experiment, including scenarios involving magnetic monopoles, highly electrically charged particles, and millicharged particles. Other contributions focus on experimental developments, highlighting novel detection techniques and technological advances aimed at identifying these unconventional signatures and probing new phenomena beyond the Standard Model.

item.title: Measurement of Born cross sections of e⁺e⁻→pK⁻Σ̅⁰ + c.c. at √(s) = 3.5-4.9 GeV and partial wave analysis at √(s) = 3.773 GeV
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using e⁺e⁻ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 44.6 fb⁻¹, we present the first measurement of the Born cross sections for the process e⁺e⁻→pK⁻Σ̅⁰ + c.c. at fifty-six center-of-mass energies between 3.51 and 4.95~GeV. By fitting the dressed cross sections of e⁺e⁻→pK⁻Σ̅⁰ + c.c. with the assumption of a power-law function plus a charmonium(-like) resonance, i.e., ψ(3770), ψ(4040), ψ(4160), Y(4230), Y(4360), ψ(4415), ψ(4500), Y(4660) or ψ(4710), no significant charmonium(-like) state decaying into pK⁻Σ̅⁰ + c.c. is observed. The product of branching fractions and electronic partial widths including their upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are provided for each decay. In addition, a partial wave analysis of the process e⁺e⁻→pK⁻Σ̅⁰ + c.c. at √(s) = 3.773 GeV is performed to investigate N^, Λ^ and Σ^* resonances in the K⁻Σ̅⁰ and pK⁻ invariant mass spectra. Significant contributions are found from the Λ(1520), Σ(1670), Σ(1915), N(1900), N(2300) and N(2570). The masses, widths and production fractions for each component are determined.

item.title: Measurement of electromagnetic transition form factors in two-photon collisions at BESIII (Max Lellmann (on behalf of the BESIII collaboration))
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The muon anomalous magnetic moment, a_μ= (g-2)_μ/2, shows a sizeable discrepancy between Standard Model (SM) predictions and direct measurements, hinting at either New Physics or limitations in modeling low-energy strong interactions. As the uncertainty in the SM predictions currently exceeds the experimental uncertainty by a substantial margin, further improvements in theoretical precision are essential to clarify the origin of this discrepancy. The SM theoretical uncertainty is dominated by hadronic processes. The hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution relies on highly accurate data for hadron production via two-photon fusion. Operating at √(s)=3.773 GeV with over 20 fb⁻¹ of integrated luminosity, the BESIII experiment is ideally suited to probe these processes at small momentum transfers. By precisely measuring channels like e⁺e⁻→e⁺ e⁻π⁰ and e⁺e⁻→e⁺ e⁻π⁰π⁰, BESIII provides the critical experimental input necessary to sharpen the SM prediction and clarify the true nature of the a_μ anomaly.

item.title: Planck-Scale Constraints on Quantum Gravity-Induced Neutrino Decoherence with IceCube
item.dc:creator: R. Abbasi et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Many quantum gravity theories predict spacetime fluctuations at the Planck scale. Neutrinos, which interact only via the weak force and gravity, propagate over long distances without losing quantum coherence. Planck-scale fluctuations would spoil that coherence, damping the flavor oscillation probability over long baselines. This makes neutrinos sensitive interferometers for Planck-scale physics. We present a search for quantum decoherence using 368,071 atmospheric neutrinos detected by IceCube in the energy range 0.5-100 TeV, an order of magnitude higher in energy than any previous decoherence search. We find no evidence for decoherence and set the strongest constraints to date on this class of neutrino decoherence models, improving on previous limits by over an order of magnitude for decoherence rate scaling as E² and E³. These results exclude natural Planck-suppressed decoherence for all energy scalings Eⁿ with 0≤n ≤3, the first such exclusion at the Planck scale for n=3.

item.title: Branching fraction measurement of the B⁰→K⁺π⁻μ⁺μ⁻ decay at high dihadron mass
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

This Letter presents the first measurement of the B⁰ →K⁺π⁻μ⁺μ⁻ differential branching fraction in the region of the dihadron K⁺π⁻ mass, m_Kπ, 1000< m_Kπ < 1835 MeV/c². This decay mode is mediated by the quark-level transition b →sℓ⁺ℓ⁻, for which the measured effective couplings show tensions with Standard Model predictions. The analysis is performed using proton-proton collision data collected with the LHCb detector between 2011 and 2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 8.4 fb⁻¹. The differential branching fraction is determined across different regions of dimuon mass squared, q², in the interval 0.1 < q² < 18.0 GeV²/c⁴, as well as in different regions of m_Kπ in the interval 1.1 < q² < 6.0 GeV²/c⁴. The results represent the first differential measurement of the branching fraction across m_Kπ within the selected dihadron-mass region, and the first observation of the decay within this region above the J/ψ resonance.

item.title: Energy-energy correlators within Z-tagged jets in proton-proton collisions at √(s) = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Energy-energy correlators probe perturbative and nonperturbative QCD regimes of jet formation through momentum-weighted angular correlations between hadrons. First measurements in light-quark-enriched jets are presented for inclusive, like-sign, and opposite-sign charged-hadron pairs, using proton-proton collisions at LHCb. The results support universality of the confinement scale for light-quark-initiated jets across collision systems and the reported transverse momentum scale of the jet. In the charge-dependent measurements, opposite-sign correlations are enhanced as angular separation decreases down to the confinement-scale region, a behavior that is well described by simulations.

item.title: Forward decay chain reconstruction with displaced vertices in intense magnetic fields
item.dc:creator: Sergio Javier Jaimes Elles et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Precise reconstruction of particle decay chains is essential for a broad range of analyses in particle physics experiments, particularly those targeting flavour physics and spectroscopy. We present a standalone, modular and extensible decay tree reconstruction framework designed to handle complicated topologies, accounting for tightly constrained particle decays and long-distance trajectory extrapolations through regions of intense and inhomogeneous magnetic field, as well as limited momentum resolution. Implemented in C++, the framework is optimised for configurability and performance. Developed primarily within CERN’s LHCb experiment, its focus is on decay chains with vertices located several metres from the LHC proton-proton interaction point, where the dipole magnetic field is maximal and non-uniform. Even so, it remains flexible: it can accommodate these special cases as well as the approximations commonly used in standard decay tree fitting tools, and the geometries of general-purpose collider detectors. Benchmark studies using simulated data demonstrate significant improvements in reconstruction efficiency, invariant mass resolution, and vertex position resolution with respect to existing tools, opening new opportunities for precision measurements and searches involving highly displaced decays.

item.title: Exploring Collective Effects in Small Collision Systems via Light-Flavour Particle Production in High-Multiplicity pp Collisions at √(s)= 13 TeV in ALICE
item.dc:creator: Rajendra Nath Patra for the ALICE Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

High-multiplicity pp and p-Pb collisions show signatures of radial and anisotropic flow, as well as the enhanced production of strange hadrons. These observations resemble phenomena seen in heavy-ion collisions, where a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is formed, although their origin in small systems remains under discussion. This contribution presents ALICE Run 2 results on light-flavour hadron (π, K, p) production in high-multiplicity (HM) pp collisions at √(s)=13 TeV, where the charged-particle multiplicity reaches values comparable to peripheral or semi-peripheral Pb-Pb collisions. The multiplicity dependence of π, K, and p transverse momentum spectra, p_T-differential and p_T-integrated particle ratios, and mean transverse momenta (⟨p_T⟩) is presented and compared with published results from other collision systems and energies, as well as with PYTHIA 8 and EPOS4 model calculations.

item.title: Detecting photons in radiative Bhabha interaction with Si-strip and LYSO crystals at future e+e- colliders
item.dc:creator: Chentao Bao et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Next-generation e+e-colliders have been proposed for the Super Tau Charm Facility covering center-of-mass energies sqrt(s) = 2-7 GeV, and for the Higgs Factories optimized for Z-pole physics and for HZ production. Luminosity can be determined by measuring forward Bhabha scattering. The QED cross-section calculation has reached a precision of better than 10^-3. Detecting radiative photons in Bhabha events provides a tool for validating higher-order corrections in theory. We propose the Forward Detector for detecting Bhabha scattering events at the STCF. The design uses high-resolution silicon detectors and finely segmented LYSO crystals to discriminate radiative photons from closely associated electrons. Bhabha scattering events are simulated with the BHLUMI and BHWIDE programs, and the detector is modeled using GEANT. Systematic uncertainties due to multiple scattering and bremsstrahlung in the beam pipe were evaluated. The potential for achieving precise measurements of radiative processes in Bhabha events is investigated.

item.title: Measurements of the branching fractions of \boldmath χ_cJ→Σ⁰Σ̅⁰η
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using (2712.4±14.3)×10⁶ ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, we report the first observations of the decay χ_cJ(J=0,1,2) →Σ⁰Σ̅⁰η. The signal significances, after considering systematic uncertainties, are determined to be 7.2σ, 5.7σ, and 6.7σ for χ_0, χ_c1, and χ_c2, respectively. The branching fractions are measured to be ℬ(χ_c0→Σ⁰Σ̅⁰η)=(9.7 ±1.7 ±0.8) ×10⁻⁵, ℬ(χ_c1→Σ⁰Σ̅⁰η)=(4.9 ±1.1 ±0.4) ×10⁻⁵, and ℬ(χ_c2→Σ⁰Σ̅⁰η)=(6.1 ±1.2 ±0.3) ×10⁻⁵, where the first uncertainties are statistical and the second systematic. No significant structure in the Σ⁰Σ̅⁰,Σ⁰η,Σ̅⁰η mass distributions is observed under the current statistics.

item.title: Measurement of the cross sections for e⁺e⁻→pn̅π⁻ at center of mass energies from 3.510 to 4.946 GeV
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 43.8~fb⁻¹ collected with the \mbox{BESIII} detector at 44 center-of-mass energy points between 3.510 and 4.946~GeV, the Born cross sections for the process e⁺e⁻ →p n̅ π⁻ and its charge-conjugated process are measured. The energy dependence of the dressed cross sections is investigated to search for possible contributions from vector charmonium and charmonium-like states. No evidence for contributions from the ψ(3770), Y(4230), Y(4360), ψ(4415), Y(4500), or Y(4710) resonances is observed. The upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are determined for the products of the electronic partial widths and the branching fractions for the decays of these resonances into the p n̅ π⁻ + c.c. final state.

item.title: Real-time Track Reconstruction with FPGAs: an example from MUonE
item.dc:creator: Michael McGinnis et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The feasibility of real-time track fitting of straight tracks for online event selection is shown in the context of the MUonE experiment. In order to reach the high throughput and low latency required for real-time track fitting, the tracking algorithm is implemented using High-Level Synthesis for an FPGA, which provides provides a balance between flexibility and performance. Hardware tracking results from a test with high-rate muons at the CERN M2 beam are presented. This test, a joint effort by the MUonE and Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiments, operated with Two-Strip (2S) modules provided by the CMS tracker group. The prototype version of the fitter used in this test achieves 3.75 μs latency and 7.75 % resource use. A comparison of the results with those obtained from a pure software implementation shows agreement well below relevant uncertainty scales. Developments since the test are also presented, with the hardware algorithm now reaching 1.35 μs latency and producing pipelined fitting results above 50 MHz while requiring less resources than the initial version. Doing so required including certain assumptions in the algorithm, but these assumptions hold for linear track fitting in general and algorithm remains useful in contexts other than MUonE.

item.title: RINO: Renormalization Group Distillation with No Labels
item.dc:creator: Zichun Hao et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Supervised machine learning in high-energy physics (HEP) requires training on labeled simulations of particle collisions, which are known to be unfaithful to the underlying physics. This leads to significant inaccuracies and biases in the transfer of trained models to real data, limiting the power of deep learning methods. Self-supervised learning (SSL) is a promising alternative for pretraining directly on real, unlabeled data. However, existing techniques largely operate with inductive biases inspired by domains such as images and natural language. We propose RINO (Renormalization Group DIstillation with NO Labels), which, for the first time, exploits the fundamentally multi-scale renormalization group structure of high-energy jet formation as a physically grounded source of SSL views. We define teacher-student representations across energy scales using different levels of hierarchical clustering, aligned via DINO-style self-distillation. To mirror the background-dominated nature of real collider data, RINO pretrains exclusively on jets from quantum chromodynamics (QCD) processes and is evaluated on out-of-distribution (OOD) transfer to rare signal classes. In our controlled data-efficiency study, RINO matches fully supervised training on JetNet after finetuning on only 1% of the labeled data. With the full labeled dataset, RINO improves OOD classification accuracy on top-quark jets by 5.9% and, without retraining, improves AUC on the unseen Higgs boson decay channel H →4q by 4.1% over the strongest SSL baseline. Scale-structure diagnostics reveal that DINO-style self-distillation permits our backbone to retain scale-dependent structure. Ablation studies show that this accounts for an 8.6% OOD accuracy gap with respect to alternative SSL paradigms such as SimCLR. Code is available at https://github.com/zichunhao/RINO.

item.title: Using Line Segment Tracking to enable ML-based Track Reconstruction in CMS
item.dc:creator: Aashay Arora on behalf of the CMS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

High-pileup conditions in CMS during the HL-LHC era make charged-particle tracking increasingly challenging as detector occupancy and combinatorics grow. We present a hybrid approach that exploits Line Segment Tracking (LST) objects rather than individual hits to enable the first CMS ML-based track reconstruction algorithm. The LST objects, namely the triplets used in this study, are built according to geometry- and physics-driven criteria and carry richer local structure, geometrical cues, and physics quantities such as transverse momentum, which helps the model incorporate detector-level information from the start. We apply a Transformer encoder with geometrically masked sparse self-attention to embed these objects in a learned latent space, and use object condensation to assemble full tracks in a single inference step. This object-based representation reduces complexity in dense environments and makes the model less sensitive to ambiguities introduced by high pileup. Evaluated on CMS Phase-2 simulation of tt̅ events at ⟨μ⟩= 200, the approach achieves reconstruction efficiency comparable to the LST quintuplet baseline while reducing the fake rate by roughly a factor of three and suppressing duplicates almost entirely, demonstrating the promise of advanced ML architectures for next-generation particle tracking.

item.title: A new AI-based Full Event Interpretation model for flavour physics
item.dc:creator: Matteo Barbieri et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The increasing event complexity and data rates foreseen for future LHC coinditions motivate a transition from selecting proton-proton (pp) collision events by reconstructing predefined signal candidates to constructing a reduced data stream by interpreting the relevant event features in a signal-agnostic way. We explore the capabilities of deep-learning-based architectures on heavy-flavour physics using LHCb as a case study. Graph-based full-event interpretation techniques address the problem by representing visible products of pp collisions as nodes of a graph, and reconstructing heavy-hadron decay chains hierarchically. A new neutral-particle-aware architecture extends the input data from charged tracks to calorimeter clusters, and uses metric learning to clusterize particles from the same decay chain in a common latent space. Tests on inclusive simulated pp→bb̅ events show that this approach retains its ability to reconstruct decay chains across a broad range of topologies and multiplicities. We discuss the resulting physics opportunities, with a focus on inclusive b→sℓℓ measurements and on searches for exotic hadrons.

item.title: Measurements of lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic B decays at Belle and Belle II (Andreas Warburton
item.dc:creator: on behalf of the Belle et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Tests of lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic \(B\)-meson decays provide sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. The Belle and Belle II experiments, respectively operating on the KEKB and SuperKEKB colliders in Japan, have collected \(e^+e^- o B ar{B}\) collisions at a center-of-mass energy corresponding to the \(\Upsilon(4S)\) resonance in samples with a combined integrated luminosity exceeding \(1\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}\). These data, with low particle multiplicity, constrained initial-state kinematics, and excellent lepton identification, provide an ideal environment to study lepton-flavour universality in semileptonic decays of \(B\) mesons. New results on the ratios of semitauonic \(B\)-decay rates compared to analogous light-lepton rates are presented. These include new Belle II measurements of branching-fraction ratios \(R(D^{(*)})\) involving exclusive \(B o D^{(*)} au u\) and \(B o D^{(*)}\ell u\) decays using semileptonic or hadronic reconstruction of the accompanying \(B\)-meson tag. Belle II and Belle measurements of angular observables in \(B o D^*\ell u\) modes that test light-lepton universality and the Lorentz structure of the decay are also presented. The measurements are statistically limited and individually consistent with Standard Model expectations. The new \(R(D^{(*)})\) results are also compatible with experimental world averages, which continue to exhibit tension with Standard Model predictions. Belle II has now accumulated an \(\Upsilon(4S)\) data sample exceeding that of Belle, offering substantial opportunities for new analysis approaches and heightened precision.

item.title: Experimental Demonstration of Soft-Tissue Muon Scattering Tomography
item.dc:creator: Dipanwita Banerjee et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Muons have fascinated physicists since their discovery in cosmic rays almost a century ago. Their large mass and relatively long lifetime allow relativistic muons to traverse large amounts of matter, a property that has been exploited to probe otherwise inaccessible structures, from volcanoes and archaeological monuments to shielded nuclear materials. Here, we experimentally demonstrate for the first time that muon scattering tomography can be extended to biological soft tissue. We image an anthropomorphic thorax phantom using a 2 GeV/c muon beam at the CERN Proton Synchrotron and reconstruct its three-dimensional scattering density from the measured deflections of individual muons. Despite the weak scattering produced by tissue-equivalent materials, the reconstructed density agrees with the expectation from simulation at the percent level. Our results extend muon imaging into a previously unexplored regime and open the possibility of using muons as a complementary probe for medical imaging.

item.title: New results from electron-positron heavy-flavor factories
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Shi
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The electron-positron heavy-flavor factories — BaBar, Belle, Belle~II, and BESIII — continue to deliver a broad and sensitive physics program. I report selected highlights presented at ICHEP 2026, covering neutral- and charged-current B processes, tests of lepton-flavor universality in b→cℓν transitions, precision measurement of Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa matrix elements, and hadron spectroscopy.

item.title: Real-time monitoring of LHCb beam spot properties based on FPGA hit reconstruction
item.dc:creator: Giulio Cordova et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present a real-time trackless method to monitor the centre of the LHCb luminous region and the relative alignment of the two halves of the LHCb Vertex Locator, using cluster counts accumulated in selected regions of the detector and processed in firmware. A Principal Component Analysis performed on simulated data yields a set of weight vectors that reduce the position estimators to scalar products of the counter rates, executable with negligible computational overhead. With pp collision data from 2024, the transverse position of the luminous region is reconstructed with a statistical precision of approximately 4 micrometre per coordinate in a 90 millisecond accumulation window. A measurement of the longitudinal centre is demonstrated with a statistical precision of a few millimetres in simulated studies. The introduction of run-time configurable firmware counters has been studied in simulation to improve the transverse and longitudinal resolutions by a factor of three with respect to the fixed-geometry baseline.

item.title: Amplitude analysis of ψ(3686) radiative decays into π⁰ π⁰ system
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A model-independent amplitude analysis of the π⁰ π⁰ system produced in radiative ψ(3686) decays is presented. The analysis is based on the unique dataset of (2712.4±14.3)×10⁶ ψ(3686) decays collected by the BESIII detector. Scalar and tensor partial-wave contributions are obtained as piecewise functions of M_inv(π⁰ π⁰⁾ with minimal model assumptions. The observed contribution of the scalar partial wave exhibits similar behavior to the one reported in the study of radiative J/ψ decays, while the tensor contributions provide no evidence for resonance-like structures except for the clearly visible f_2(1270). The results are presented in the form of log-likelihood scans in M_inv(π⁰ π⁰⁾ bins, which preserve all the statistical information and account for relevant systematic uncertainties. The model-independent description provided in this paper allows to combine the presented results with other related data in the development of phenomenological models.

item.title: Probing the proton structure with minimum bias and low-pt dimuon events at hadron colliders
item.dc:creator: Kyle Cormier
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

This paper presents two methods for probing the proton structure and the number of partonic interactions in proton-proton collisions using dimuon production and minimum bias events. At the LHC these targeted measurements can provide information on the average number of partonic scatters in different event classes, their dependence on the partonic momentum fraction, x, and potentially partonic flavour. Within a simple mostly geometric model of multiparton interactions as quasi-independent scatters, the measurements can be used to make inference about the proton-proton overlap dependence on impact parameter and its partonic-x dependence.

item.title: \textbf{\textsc{HepUKE}}: Uncertainty-aware Knowledge Evolution for High Energy Physics Analysis Agents
item.dc:creator: Zijie Shang et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Knowledge bases are essential to agents for high energy physics (HEP), supplying few-shot evidence for previously unseen tasks. Their principal utility lies in strategic guidance for novel analyses rather than ready-made answers or reusable code. Prevailing systems, however, treat all retrieved evidence as equally trustworthy and fail to accrue knowledge from the analyses under assistance. In this paper, inspired by the standard HEP treatment of uncertainty, we propose \textbf{\textsc{\underline{HepUKE}}}: an \textbf{\underline{U}}ncertainty-aware \textbf{\underline{K}}nowledge \textbf{\underline{E}}volution system for \textbf{\underline{HEP}} that repurposes information entropy to unify statistical uncertainty from LLM generation and systematic uncertainty from HEP methodological choices. Upon it, we construct a self-evolving domain-specific-language (DSL) knowledge base and release a large-scale expert-annotated HEP physics-analysis benchmark. Per-evidence confidence is quantified via the information entropy of sampled DSL generations: high-confidence precedents constrain program synthesis, whereas analyses lacking close precedents are validated and written back, sustaining continual knowledge evolution. To handle the highly redundant yet logically stringent nature of HEP knowledge, we introduce an early-stopping controller that fuses a backward stationarity test on the answer posterior with a forward marginal information gain estimate. On the 1,000-pair BESIII PhysicsQA benchmark, HepUKE reduces retrieval rounds by 43.0\% while preserving most answer quality, and on the out-of-domain HotpotQA benchmark, it reduces retrieval rounds by 14.5\% with a similar quality–efficiency trade-off. The code and datasets used in this work are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HepUKE-32FF.

item.title: Observation of a Threshold Enhancement in the π⁰π⁰ Mass Spectrum in ψ(3686) →π⁰π⁰J/ψ Decays
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using a data sample of (2712.4±14.4)×10⁶ ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector, we report a high-precision study of the π⁰π⁰ mass spectrum from ψ(3686)→π⁰π⁰J/ψ decays. The enhancement previously observed near the ππ mass threshold in the π⁺π⁻ channel is confirmed, with a statistical significance exceeding 10σ. A fit with a Breit-Wigner function yields a mass of M = 274.3±2.1_stat.±0.6_syst. MeV/c² and a width of Γ= 17.1±1.5_stat.±0.5_syst. MeV, consistent with those from the π⁺π⁻ channel. By including final-state interactions, we analyze the data using both chiral perturbation theory (ChPT) and QCD multipole expansion (QCDME). While the ChPT model describes the higher-mass region above 0.3 GeV/c² well, it fails to reproduce the significant threshold enhancement. In contrast, the QCDME model, which incorporates the S- and D-wave admixture structure of ψ(3686), provides a better description of the full π⁰π⁰ mass spectrum.

item.title: Determination of U-spin breaking parameters with an amplitude analysis of the decay D⁰→K_S,L⁰π⁺π⁻
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We perform a simultaneous amplitude analysis of the decays D⁰ →K_S⁰π⁺π⁻ and D⁰ →K_L⁰π⁺π⁻ using an e⁺e⁻ collision data sample, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 20.3 fb⁻¹, collected at the centre-of-mass energy of 3.773 GeV with the BESIII detector. This study, based on a significantly larger dataset than that used in previous work, presents an updated measurement of the complex U-spin breaking parameters (ρ̂) associated with various CP eigenstate resonant modes mediating the three-body decays. The magnitudes of the ρ̂ parameters range from 0.62 to 4.45, indicating substantial U-spin symmetry breaking. We also report the resonant fit fraction and obtain a model prediction for the average strong-phase parameters over regions of phase space for both decay modes.

item.title: Recent results in b →s ℓℓ transitions at LHCb
item.dc:creator: Juan Jose Juan Castella
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Rare decays of B hadrons, such as b→sℓℓ processes, provide great avenues to search for the influence of new physics (NP). They are highly suppressed in the Standard Model (SM) and therefore sensitive to NP contributions. In recent years, experimental measurements have shown tension with SM predictions. It is still up for debate whether these stem from genuine NP or an incomplete understanding of the theory. These proceedings focus on the recent efforts of the LHCb collaboration to advance this field. Some of the results covered show that tensions in these processes, like in B⁰ →K^0 μ⁺ μ⁻, still persist upon higher precision. Others aim to shed some light on the theoretical picture through amplitude analyses of decays like B⁰ →K^0 μ⁺ μ⁻ and B⁺ →K⁺ μ⁺ μ⁻. We also present two innovative measurements: the branching fraction of B⁰ →K⁺ π⁻ μ⁺ μ⁻ at large dihadron mass; and the first hadron collider measurement of the lepton flavour universality ratio of B⁰ →K^*0 ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ at high q² (dilepton mass squared).

item.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at √(s) = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb⁻¹. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high p_T. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

item.title: Tau and dark sector searches at Belle and Belle II
item.dc:creator: Wenzhe Li
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The Belle and Belle II experiments provide a powerful platform for beyond-the-Standard-Model searches, particularly in tau and dark sectors. This summary reports include a measurement of CP violation in τ⁻ →π⁻ K_S⁰ ν_τ, a search for τ⁻ →ℓ⁻ η, a search for axion-like particles via e⁺ e⁻ →γa (→γγ) using Belle II data, and a search for feebly interacting particles in B →h X_inv decays using Belle data.

item.title: Observation of single top-quark production in the s-channel in proton--proton collisions at √(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The first single-experiment observation of single top-quark production in the s-channel is presented. Measurements of this process are essential to fully characterize the electroweak interactions of the top quark and probe for new physics, however its highly suppressed cross-section has so far caused it to evade direct detection at the Large Hadron Collider. The analysis uses proton–proton collision data collected at a center-of-mass energy of √(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 140 fb⁻¹. The selected events contain exactly one electron or muon, missing transverse momentum, and exactly two b-quark-initiated jets. A Graph Neural Network is utilized to separate the signal from the top-quark pair, W+jets, and t-channel single top-quark backgrounds. A likelihood fit to the network output yields an observed (expected) signal significance of 5.1 (5.2) standard deviations. The measured cross-section of σ_tb̅+t̅b = 10.8 ±1.5 (stat.) ±1.6 (syst.) pb is consistent with the Standard Model prediction.

item.title: Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND): Design and Initial Performance
item.dc:creator: SBND Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) is a 112 tonne active mass liquid argon time projection chamber (LArTPC) situated in the Booster Neutrino Beam at Fermilab, forming part of the Short-Baseline Neutrino (SBN) Program. SBND began operation in 2024 and has since accumulated the world’s largest sample of neutrino-argon interactions. This paper describes the as-built detector and presents performance results from the first year of beam operation. All detector systems performed at or above design requirements. The liquid argon purity achieved an electron lifetime exceeding 30ms, ten times the design requirement, for more than 95% of Run 1. The TPC wire plane readout achieved noise levels at the theoretical minimum for the given wire geometry (an average of 388e⁻ for the 4m long collection plane wires) with 99.3% of readout channels live. Together, the liquid argon purity and TPC performance are enabling extremely clean event reconstruction in the SBND TPC. The photon detection system, consisting of passive reflectors and multiple active components (PMTs and X-ARAPUCAs), has achieved a light yield exceeding 10 photoelectrons per MeV throughout the detector volume and a timing resolution of a few nanoseconds, sufficient to resolve the 19ns bunch structure of the Booster Neutrino Beam. A nearly 4π cosmic ray tagger system surrounds the TPC to mitigate cosmic backgrounds in neutrino and BSM physics analyses. The data acquisition system has demonstrated stable performance up to an event rate of 8Hz, and a data collection efficiency of 98.6% was achieved throughout SBND’s first neutrino run in 2025. These results demonstrate that SBND represents the state of the art in multi-tonne-scale LArTPC detector performance.

item.title: Observation of χ_cJ→ΛK⁰_SΞ̅⁰ + c.c. and improved measurements of χ_cJ→ΛK⁻Ξ̅⁺ + c.c.
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

By analyzing (2712.4±14.3)×10⁶ ψ(3686) events collected with the BESIII detector operating at the BEPCII collider, we report the first observation of χ_cJ→ΛK⁰_SΞ̅⁰ + c.c. (J=0,1,2) with significances greater than 10σ, including systematic uncertainties, and improved measurements of χ_cJ→ΛK⁻Ξ̅⁺ + c.c. The branching fractions of these decays are determined to be ℬ(χ_c0→ΛK⁰_SΞ̅⁰⁺c.c.)=(1.13±0.13±0.13)×10⁻⁴, ℬ(χ_c1→ΛK⁰_SΞ̅⁰⁺c.c.)=(0.74±0.08±0.07)×10⁻⁴, ℬ(χ_c2→ΛK⁰_SΞ̅⁰⁺c.c.)=(1.16±0.11±0.14)×10⁻⁴, ℬ(χ_c0→ΛK⁻Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c.)=(1.90±0.08±0.16)×10⁻⁴, ℬ(χ_c1→ΛK⁻Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c.)=(1.40±0.05±0.11)×10⁻⁴, and ℬ(χ_c2→ΛK⁻Ξ̅⁺⁺c.c.)=(1.95±0.07±0.15)×10⁻⁴. The first uncertainties are statistical, and the second are systematic.

item.title: Using Geometric Deep Learning for the Detection of the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background in Water-Cherenkov Detectors
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Melennec et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The study of the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background (DSNB) is an essential approach to improve our understanding of the formation of Core-Collapse Supernovae, as well as investigating fundamental neutrino properties. The detection of the DSNB flux however is a difficult task, as it requires the disentanglement of its signal with many competitive backgrounds in the low energy range. The main DSNB detection channel is the Inverse Beta Decay (IBD), which is characterised by a distinct, time-separated two-signal signature. This work introduces the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to handle critical detection and reconstruction tasks for the DSNB through the IBD channel. In particular, we present a model to recover the energy of the first signal from a low energy positron. Additionally, we develop a signal-to-background classifier optimised for the secondary signal, which corresponds to the characteristic photon emission following a neutron capture event. We test our models on two simulations in a Hyper-Kamiokande-like water Cherenkov detector geometry, and show that we obtain performances that are comparable to the state of the art.

item.title: Optimising Geometric Deep Learning for Varied Reconstruction Tasks in High Granularity Calorimeters
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Melennec et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

In the recent years, high energy physics discoveries have been driven by the increasing of luminosity and/or detector granularity. This evolution gives access to bigger statistics and data samples, but can make it hard to process the detector outputs with current methods and algorithms. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), have been shown to be powerful tools to address these challenges. While GNNs can deal with the non-euclidean nature of the data extracted from these detectors, their deployment presents significant difficulties, mainly from the computational complexity of the algorithms they are based on. We propose to use the known geometries of the detectors to optimise the algorithms used for GNN pipelines, which usually have quadratic algorithmic complexities. We validate the validity of our optimised approach on various tasks, such as particle identification, energy regression and instance segmentation. Finally, we present HIBOU, a generic modular architecture that provides a blueprint for how these GNN blocks are to be implemented within experiment-specific reconstruction frameworks.

item.title: Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments
item.dc:creator: Miaochen Jin et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present a combined analysis of the latest publicly available atmospheric neutrino data from Super-Kamiokande including all data-taking stages previous to the gadolinium phase, IceCube-DeepCore, and the six-detection-unit configuration of KM3NeT/ORCA. Our fit uses all event samples simultaneously and treats the systematic uncertainties shared among experiments as fully correlated, while detector-response uncertainties are modeled independently for each experiment. %We measure The combined data constrain the atmospheric oscillation parameters to Δm²_31 = 2.44⁺⁰.06_-0.04 ×10⁻³ eV² and sin²θ_23 = 0.52⁺⁰.03_-0.04, with a precision of 2.2% and 6.1%, respectively, which is competitive with current accelerator-based measurements, and independently constrain the CP-violating phase to δ_CP = 1.30⁺⁰.24_-0.28 π. Finally, comparing the orderings of the neutrino mass spectrum, we find a preference for the normal ordering with Δχ² = 11.0; further calibrated with pseudoexperiments, we exclude the inverted ordering at 99.95% confidence level (3.3σ).

item.title: A compact, interrogable Tree Tensor Network Jet Tagger on Lund declustering trees
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Napolitano et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Jet taggers built on the Lund declustering tree encode QCD radiation structure in the inputs and process it with graph networks. We ask whether the tree itself can also constrain the computation, and what becomes accessible when it does. For this, we construct a novel quantum-inspired Tree Tensor Network (TTN), where a single tensor core is shared among the internal nodes of the Cambridge/Aachen declustering tree, employing Lund coordinates, and with no particle-identification or detector-level information. The construction is based on a strong prior on the radiation history rather than on the constituents, complementary to compact equivariant taggers. Because the same learned map acts identically at every node, the trained model can be evaluated on truncated trees and its latent space compared across recursions, and used to localise where on the Lund jet plane the Pythia and Herwig jet representations diverge, showing the regions of generator-dependent concentration. The χ=8 model has 4014 trainable parameters against approximately 391,000 for LundNet. We evaluate boosted top tagging and quark/gluon discrimination at particle level on Pythia and Herwig samples, in both native (Pythia→Pythia) and transfer (Pythia→Herwig) configurations. Despite differing in capacity by two orders of magnitude, the TTN reaches native performance close to LundNet in quark/gluon discrimination, slightly underperforming in top tagging, with a similar Pythia-to-Herwig transfer behavior in both tasks. Finally, we show the behavior of the network as a function of the bond dimension, and as a function of the perturbative scale.

item.title: Observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz transition J/ψ→e⁺ e⁻ η_c
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Using (10.087±0.044)×10⁹ J/ψ events collected with the BESIII detector at the e⁺e⁻ BEPCII collider, we present the first observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay J/ψ→e⁺ e⁻ η_c. The relative branching fraction R ≡Γ(J/ψ→e⁺e⁻η_c)/Γ(J/ψ→γη_c) is determined to be (0.65±0.02_stat.±0.07_sys.)%, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. The q²-dependent form factors are also extracted, and no significant deviation from the theoretical prediction is seen.

item.title: Green's functions and weighting fields for dielectric multilayer geometries
item.dc:creator: Werner Riegler
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The electrostatic potential of a point charge in a geometry with an arbitrary number of parallel layers of different permittivity, bounded by two grounded planes, is derived. Different boundary conditions in the transverse direction are discussed. For the case where a grounded plane is segmented into strips and pads, the solution is used to derive the weighting fields for these electrodes.

item.title: First observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay ψ(3686) →μ⁺ μ⁻ η^'
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Utilizing (2712.4 ± 14.3)×10⁶ ψ(3686) events collected by the BESIII detector at the symmetric e⁺ e⁻ collider BEPCII, we report the first observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay ψ(3686) →μ⁺ μ⁻η^’ with a statistical significance of 6.1σ. The branching fraction is determined to be ℬ(ψ(3686) →μ⁺ μ⁻ η^’)=(4.1 ±1.0_stat. ±0.4_syst.)×10⁻⁷. The ratio to the branching fraction of the radiative decay ψ(3686) →γη^’ is estimated to be (3.3±0.9)×10⁻³, which is consistent with the prediction of the vector meson dominance model within 1σ. Furthermore, using the branching fraction of ψ(3686) →e⁺ e⁻ η^’ previously measured by the BESIII experiment, the ratio between the muon and the electron channels is evaluated to be 0.22±0.07, which is consistent with the calculation of the vector meson dominance model within 1σ, and no significant violation of lepton flavor universality is found.

item.title: Search for rare charm decays at BESIII
item.dc:creator: Xiaokang Li et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The BESIII experiment searches for rare and symmetry-violating decays with the largest charmonium and threshold open-charm data samples. This contribution reviews recent searches for charmonium weak decays, charm flavour-changing neutral currents, charged-lepton flavour violation, and Bose-symmetry violation. The weak-decay searches have improved several branching-fraction limits, while studies of rare charm-meson and charmonium decays probe flavour-changing neutral currents. Searches for charged-lepton flavour violation set limits in vector and pseudoscalar meson decays and constrain effective interactions. No significant signals are found in any of these searches. The neutral-kaon limits fall below the expectations of a proposed locality scenario, and the J/ψ limit approaches the scale predicted for Standard Model CP violation.

item.title: HybridMC: a fast detailed simulation framework for optical calorimeter technologies at the LHCb ECAL Upgrade II
item.dc:creator: Marco Pizzichemi et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The detailed Monte Carlo simulation of optical calorimeters is dominated by the generation and tracking of scintillation and Cherenkov photons, which in standard Geant4 ray-tracing increases the CPU time per electromagnetic shower by up to three orders of magnitude compared to simulating only the energy deposition. At the luminosity and granularity foreseen for the LHCb ECAL Upgrade II, this cost becomes prohibitive for both detector R&D and large-scale sample production. The optical photons cannot simply be discarded, because the time resolution of a few tens of picoseconds targeted by the upgrade to mitigate pile-up is driven by their arrival-time distribution at the photo-detectors. This paper presents HybridMC, a fast and detailed simulation framework for optical calorimeters that decouples shower development from optical transport. Energy deposition is handled by a standard Geant4 simulation without optical photon propagation, while light transport is reproduced by a parametrised summary Monte Carlo step based on probability density functions extracted from a one-time full ray-tracing optical calibration. A Monte Carlo-to-Monte Carlo validation shows good statistical agreement with full ray-tracing for all module types of the upgraded LHCb ECAL, from individual photon arrival times up to the reconstructed energy and time resolutions. The CPU time is reduced by more than two orders of magnitude, with module-dependent acceleration factors from 150 to 480. A comparison to test-beam data from DESY II and the CERN SPS shows that the framework reproduces the momentum dependence of the measured energy and time resolutions of a real prototype, up to a small residual constant term. HybridMC retains the microscopic optical detail not accessible to flash simulators based on generative models, at a CPU cost compatible with large-scale production on standard computing infrastructure.

item.title: Gain fluctuations in a uniform avalanche diode
item.dc:creator: Werner Riegler
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We derive the explicit probability distribution of the total avalanche size produced by m primary electron-hole pairs created at an arbitrary position in a uniform avalanche diode. We also derive an operator that generates all raw moments.

item.title: Simultaneous measurement of the Higgs boson decay rates to WW and ZZ in fully hadronic final states at FCC-ee
item.dc:creator: Jan Eysermans et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

The precise determination of the Higgs boson couplings to electroweak gauge bosons is a key objective of the FCC-ee physics program. In particular, measurements of the Higgs boson couplings to W and Z bosons play a central role in the model-independent determination of its total decay width. This paper presents a study of Higgs boson decays to H -> WW and H -> ZZ in the Higgsstrahlung production process. The analysis focuses on events in which the associated Z boson and the vector bosons from the Higgs decay all decay hadronically, resulting in six-jet final states. The large H -> WW branching fraction leads to high signal statistics in the fully hadronic channel, while for H -> ZZ the much smaller Higgs branching fraction is partly compensated by the large hadronic branching fractions of the Z bosons. Due to the substantial kinematic overlap between the WW and ZZ decay modes, their signal strengths are extracted simultaneously. Jet-clustering and dedicated jet-pairing techniques are employed to optimize the reconstruction of the hadronically decaying gauge bosons and enhance the separation of the two signal components. Assuming a center-of-mass energy of 240 GeV and an integrated luminosity of 10.8 ab^-1, expected relative uncertainties of 1.48% and 8.20% are obtained on the production cross section times branching fraction, sigma(ZH) x BR, for the H -> WW and H -> ZZ decay modes, respectively.

item.title: Search for Higgs boson compositeness effects in high-mass dilepton final states in proton-proton collisions at √(s) = 13 and 13.6 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

A search for beyond the standard model effects in high-mass dielectron and dimuon final states with the CMS detector is performed, with a specific focus on Higgs boson compositeness. The search uses data collected at the LHC at 13 and 13.6 TeV center-of-mass energies, corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 207 fb⁻¹. Compositeness would manifest as distortions in the observed dilepton mass spectrum and the presence of bound states, such as the Higgs boson and new massive vector boson resonances. Assuming the existence of new boson states with masses well above the TeV scale, an effective field theory approach provides stringent bounds on the oblique parameters 𝒲 and 𝒴, which are zero in the standard model. One-dimensional fits, in which only one of the oblique parameters is allowed to deviate from zero, provide the following limits: -3.9 × 10⁻⁴ 𝒴 3.5 × 10⁻⁴ and -2.1 × 10⁻⁴ 𝒲 1.6 × 10⁻⁴ at 95% confidence level. More stringent compositeness limits at the TeV scale are set in several new physics scenarios under the assumption that a new Z’ resonance is physically present within or slightly above the visible dilepton mass spectrum. In this context, cases with large resonance decay widths are explored for the first time.

item.title: Observation of D⁺ →K^*0ρ⁺ and D⁺→K^*+ρ⁰ in Doubly Cabibbo-Suppressed Decay D⁺ →K⁺π⁺π⁻π⁰
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

By analyzing an e⁺e⁻ collision data sample with an integrated luminosity of 20.3 fb⁻¹ collected with the BESIII detector at the center-of-mass energy of 3.773 GeV, we perform the first amplitude analysis on the doubly Cabibbo-suppressed decay D⁺ →K⁺π⁺π⁻π⁰ and report the first observation of D⁺ →K^0ρ⁺ and D⁺→K^+ρ⁰. The corresponding branching fractions are (5.67±0.41_stat±0.17_syst)×10⁻⁴ and (5.32±0.57_stat±0.24_syst)×10⁻⁴, respectively. These two D→VV decay both have large transverse polarizations. The longitudinal polarization fractions are measured to be 0.111±0.024_stat±0.008_syst and 0.263±0.049_stat±0.015_syst, respectively. The branching fraction of the decay D⁺→K⁺ω is measured to be (4.76±0.84_stat±0.13_syst)×10⁻⁵.

item.title: Precision measurement of ocean tides using cosmic-ray muons
item.dc:creator: Jiwon Seo et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Cosmic-ray muons provide a natural probe of the integrated mass along their trajectories. Here we show that cosmic-ray muons can monitor ocean-tide-induced variations in seawater overburden within an underwater tunnel. The observed modulation closely tracks independent tide-gauge measurements, yielding an attenuation response coefficient of k=43.2±1.0~counts/h/m and resolving meter-scale variations in seawater overburden. A spatial muography scan validates the overburden model, confirming that the seawater contribution is essential to reproduce the observed attenuation. Unlike conventional tide gauges that measure sea level locally, muography measures the integrated overburden above the detector. These results demonstrate that muography can quantitatively resolve small, time-dependent variations in environmental overburden, providing a new approach to monitoring dynamic natural systems.

item.title: Search for Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background of All Flavors with PandaX-4T
item.dc:creator: Yingxin Zhang et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

We present the first search for the diffuse supernova neutrino background utilizing coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering with the PandaX-4T liquid xenon detector at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory. Based on a total exposure of 1.54 tonne ·year from the commissioning and first science runs, we observe no significant event excess over the expected background. We therefore set an upper limit of (2.27 - 2.43) ×10³ cm⁻²s⁻¹ per flavor at 90\% confidence level on the ν_x flux (each of ν_μ, ν̅_μ, ν_τ, ν̅_τ) of the diffuse supernova neutrino background for incident neutrino energies above 19.3~MeV. The result is comparable to the current world best limit.

item.title: A graph neural network for deep learning-based full event interpretation at FCC-ee
item.dc:creator: Elena Graverini et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

This paper presents a deep learning-based full event interpretation prototype developed for the electron-positron Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee) using simulated e⁺e⁻→Z→bb̅ events at √(s) = 91 GeV. The study was carried out using the Innovative Detector for Electron positron Accelerators (IDEA) detector concept as case study for future application. The proposed graph neural network framework aims to simultaneously identify and reconstruct the hierarchical decay trees of b-hadrons in each event using information from reconstructed charged particles. Events are represented as graphs, where reconstructed charged particles form the nodes and pairwise observables are encoded as edge features describing the relations between particles. On a test sample, 90% of reconstructed decay chains contain exactly the correct set of particles, irrespective of their inferred decay hierarchy. Across a range of benchmark b-hadron decays, this clustering efficiency exceeds 93% for decay chains spanning up to three generations of decays.

item.title: SysVar: Consistent and scalable treatment of systematic uncertainties in template-based analyses
item.dc:creator: Ilias Tsaklidis et al.
item.description:
New hep-ex announcement — original abstract; no AI summary.

Propagating systematic uncertainties from correction weights into templates generated from simulated data while preserving correlations in the signal extraction variables becomes increasingly challenging as analyses scale in size. SysVar’s lightweight API hides most of the bookkeeping complexity of applying correction weights, building systematic variations, and histogramming nominal and varied templates. This streamlines workflows that are otherwise error-prone but essential for high-precision measurements. Correlations are preserved by propagating the full covariance across the analysis and compressing it into a small set of orthogonal eigenvariations, each defining an ordinary shape nuisance parameter. In this work, we demonstrate SysVar’s workflow and impact by combining two independent pseudo-measurements that benefit from consistently correlated systematic uncertainties encoded in the template shapes.
